Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 29, verses 1–7:

Explanation of the words:

Alif Lam Mim: This is one of the disjointed letters (al-huruf al-muqatta'a). It is written Alif Lam Mim (الۤمۤ) and read "alif lam meem."

And they will not be tried: by that which shows the truth of their faith from the obligations, among them patience upon harm.

And We did certainly try those before them: that is, We tested those before them, for this is a continuing practice (sunnah jariyah) among people.

So that Allah will surely know those who were truthful: that is, in their faith; and He will surely know the liars in it by what appears of their deeds.

Outrun us: that is, escape Us so that We do not take vengeance upon them.

Evil is what they judge: that is, wretched is this judgment they make, which is their assumption that they can escape Allah the Exalted and that He is not able to take vengeance upon them.

Whoever hopes for the meeting with Allah: that is, whoever believes in the meeting with Allah and awaits its occurrence, let him know that his term (ajal) is surely coming, and let him prepare for it with faith and righteous deeds.

And whoever strives: that is, exerts effort in fighting the disbelievers or the self.

Then he strives only for himself: that is, the benefit of the striving, in the form of reward, returns to himself.

And We will surely reward them with the best: that is, and We will surely reward them for their deeds with the best deed they had done.

Meaning of the verses:

Alif Lam Mim: Allah knows best what He means by it. This is the position of the early pious predecessors (al-salaf) regarding these letters, which is to entrust their knowledge to the One who revealed them, Mighty and Majestic. His saying ﴿Do people think﴾ means: do people suppose ﴿that they will be left to say, "We believe," and they will not be tried?﴾ That is, they will not be tested. Rather, there must be a testing by arduous obligations such as emigration, striving, prayer, fasting, zakat, abstaining from desires, and patience upon harm. Although the verse was revealed concerning people like Ammar ibn Yasir, Bilal and Ayyash, its meaning is general, since the lesson lies in the generality of the wording and not in the specificity of the cause, and the wording here is general because a noun of kind (ism al-jins), when preceded by "al," conveys the encompassing of all its members. His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿And We did certainly try those before them﴾ refers to the earlier nations. Thus it is an established practice (sunnah maddiyah) among people that does not fail.

His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿So that Allah will surely know those who were truthful﴾ in their faith, meaning that this becomes manifest and He knows it by observation, after He had known it before bringing it into existence, since He had decreed it and recorded it in the Book of Decrees. This occurs through their being charged with obligations and fulfilling what they were charged with, of difficult actions and difficult abstentions, since emigration, striving and zakat are actions, while abstaining from usury, adultery and wine are abstentions. ﴿And He will surely know the liars﴾ who claimed faith, and when they were tested with obligations they did not fulfill them, so their untruthfulness became evident and that they are liars in their claim to be believers.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Or do those who commit evil deeds think that they can outrun Us?﴾ That is, do ﴿those who commit evil deeds﴾ of shirk and sins suppose ﴿that they can outrun Us﴾, that is, escape Us, so that We do not seize them with punishment. ﴿Evil is what they judge﴾ for themselves, meaning that their judgment is wretched, because it is corrupt, since they founded it on the assumption that Allah, Exalted is He, has no power over them, while He is capable of all things, and that He does not know them, while He is knowing of all things.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Whoever hopes for the meeting with Allah – then indeed the term of Allah is coming﴾ means: whoever believes and hopes for the meeting with Allah, which is the Day of Resurrection, let him know that the term Allah has set for that is certainly coming. Accordingly, let him prepare for His meeting with what suits it, which is faith and righteous deeds after abandoning shirk and corrupt deeds. From here, a person's claim that he hopes to meet his Lord while he does no righteous deed for which he is rewarded is a claim that is not valid. Allah said in Surat al-Kahf: ﴿...Whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous deeds and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord﴾ [Verse 110]. His saying ﴿And He is the Hearing, the Knowing﴾ means that He, Exalted is He, hears the words of His servants and knows their intentions and deeds. So a claim of faith, whether outward from the servant or inward, has no worth unless its holder establishes proof for it, and that is by faith and by striving against the outward and inward enemy.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And whoever strives, he strives only for himself﴾ means that the benefit of this act of worship returns to the servant himself, whereas Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is absolutely free of the deeds of His servants, an absolute independence, as indicated by His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is free of need from the worlds﴾, meaning the angels, humans, jinn and all other creatures, since everything other than Allah Exalted is a world (alam), and its plural is awalim and alamin. His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And those who believe and do righteous deeds – We will surely remove from them their misdeeds﴾ is a promise from Allah Exalted to whoever of His servants believes and does righteous deeds, both in action and abstention, that He will expiate from him the misdeeds he committed before Islam and after it. The meaning of expiating them is that He covers and conceals them and does not hold them to account for them, as if they had never done them. His saying ﴿And We will surely reward them﴾ means for their righteous deeds ﴿with the best﴾, that is, with the best deed they had done, so that it is multiplied to the greatest extent. This is from His generosity toward His righteous servants, that He rewards a good deed with many times its equivalent, hundreds of times over.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- Explanation of the established practice that faith is confirmed or refuted by deeds.

2- Explanation that it is possible to be charged with what is hard for the self to do or to abstain from, but not with what is beyond its capacity.

3- A warning to the deluded against punishment, even if it is delayed for a time, for it will certainly befall.

4- The fruit of striving returns to the striver himself. Therefore he should not place it as a favor upon Allah by saying, "I did such and such."

5- Affirmation of the doctrine of resurrection and recompense, by mentioning the promise to those who believe and do righteous deeds of expiation of misdeeds and the best reward, which will be fulfilled on the Day of Resurrection.

**Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 29, Verses 8–13**

**Explanation of the Words:**

"And We enjoined upon man": i.e., We charged him through the revelation sent down to Our Messenger.

"Good treatment toward his parents": i.e., an injunction of goodness, namely, dutifulness to them and not disobeying them.

"And if they strive with you": i.e., they both exerted their utmost effort to make you associate partners with Him.

"We will surely admit them among the righteous": i.e., We will admit them to their place in Paradise.

"The trial of people": i.e., their harm to him.

"Like the punishment of Allah": i.e., in fear of them, so that he obeys them and becomes a hypocrite.

"Indeed, we were with you": i.e., in faith, and we were only compelled to say what we said with our tongues.

"Follow our way": i.e., our religion and what we follow.

"And let us bear your sins": i.e., let there be from you the following of our way and from us the bearing of your sins. The statement is a report, not a command.

"And they will surely bear their burdens": i.e., their sins, and "sins" means wrongdoings.

"And burdens along with their burdens": i.e., because of their saying to the believers, "Follow our way."

"Concerning what they used to fabricate": i.e., what they used to lie about.

**The Meaning of the Verses:**

These verses were revealed concerning Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas. When he embraced Islam, his mother, Hamnah bint Abi Sufyan, said to him: "What is this religion you have innovated? By Allah, I will neither eat nor drink until you return to what you were upon, or I die, and you will be reproached for it forever; it will be said, 'O slayer of his mother!'" She remained for a day and a night without eating, drinking, or seeking shade, and she became exhausted. Then she remained another day and night without eating or drinking. Sa'd came to her and said: "O mother, even if you had a hundred souls and they departed one by one, I would not abandon my religion. So eat if you wish, and if you wish, do not eat." When she despaired of him, she embraced Islam, ate, and drank. Then Allah revealed this verse: ﴿And We enjoined upon man goodness toward his parents﴾, i.e., We charged him, through the messengers, with an injunction of goodness, which is to honor them by obeying them in what is right, and to refrain from harming them even slightly, and to convey every good to them, whether in word or deed. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if they strive with you﴾, i.e., they both exerted their utmost effort to make you associate with Me anything of associating partners, or partners, then do not obey them, as Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas did with his mother by not obeying her. His saying ﴿To Me is your return﴾, [both] children and parents, ﴿and I will inform you of what you used to do﴾ and recompense you for it. Therefore, they should give precedence to My obedience over the obedience of parents, for it is I who will account for you and recompense you for your deeds, you and them alike. His exalted saying: ﴿And those who believed﴾, i.e., in Allah and His Messenger, ﴿and did righteous deeds﴾, which are the acts of worship through which Allah, exalted is He, has worshipped His believing servants. He prescribed them and His Messenger ﷺ explained them, such as remembrance, recitation of the Qur'an, prayer, fasting, charity, struggle (jihad), pilgrimage, and whatever is similar to these. These are the ones who combined true faith with righteous deeds free of associating partners and showing off. Allah, exalted is He, swears that He will admit them into the company of the righteous, namely the prophets and the saints, in Paradise, the Abode of Peace (Dar al-Salam).

His exalted saying: ﴿And among the people is one who says, "We believe in Allah"﴾, the verse. This was revealed concerning people in Makkah who believed and declared their faith, so the polytheists persecuted them, and they became hypocrites. Allah, exalted is He, informed about them with His saying: ﴿And among the people is one who says, "We believe in Allah," but when he is harmed for the sake of Allah﴾, i.e., when the polytheists harmed him, he turned to hypocrisy and apostasy, ﴿he regards the trial of people﴾, i.e., their harm to him and their torment of him, ﴿as the punishment of Allah﴾ on the Day of Resurrection. Thus he agreed with the polytheists in disbelief.

His exalted saying: ﴿And if victory comes from your Lord, they will surely say, "Indeed, we were with you"﴾, i.e., in faith, and we were only compelled. This was revealed concerning those who went out from Makkah to Badr with the polytheists. When the polytheists were routed, the Muslims were victorious and took prisoners, they said, ﴿Indeed, we were with you,﴾ i.e., in faith. Allah, exalted is He, refuted their claim with His saying: ﴿Is not Allah most knowing of what is within the breasts of the worlds?﴾, i.e., of the people. His exalted saying: ﴿And Allah will surely make evident those who believed, and He will surely make evident the hypocrites﴾ confirms what preceded in the previous verse, and it entails the recompense for faith and for hypocrisy. His knowledge, exalted is He, necessitates a just recompense: the people of faith He will recompense with lasting bliss, and the people of hypocrisy with humiliating punishment. Those are in the Abode of Peace, and these are in the Abode of Ruin (Dar al-Bawar).

His exalted saying: ﴿And those who disbelieved said to those who believed, "Follow our way"﴾, i.e., our religion and what we are upon, ﴿and we will bear your sins.﴾ i.e., the leaders of Quraysh said to some of the believers: "Abandon the way of Muhammad and his religion and follow our way and our religion. And even if there is a resurrection and recompense, as Muhammad ﷺ says, we are ready to bear your sins, and to be recompensed for them instead of you." So Allah, exalted is He, refuted them with His saying: ﴿And they will not bear anything of their sins at all﴾, and ﴿Indeed, they are liars﴾ in their saying, "and we will bear your sins." Allah, exalted is He, said, swearing by His might and majesty: ﴿And they will surely bear their own burdens﴾, i.e., their sins, ﴿and burdens along with their burdens﴾, i.e., additional sins along with their sins which are their own wrongdoings, and this is because of what they said to them. ﴿And they will surely be questioned on the Day of Resurrection about what they used to fabricate﴾, i.e., what they used to lie about, namely, that they would bear the sins of the believers on the Day of Resurrection.

**Guidance of the Verses:**

1. The obligation of dutifulness to parents in what is right, and not obeying them in what is forbidden, such as associating partners with Allah and sinning.

2. Glad tidings for believers who do righteous deeds, that they will be admitted into Paradise along with the prophets and the truthful.

3. Condemnation of hypocrisy and the disbelief of hypocrites, even if they claim to be believers, for they are not believers.

4. Description of the extreme disbelief and tyranny of the arrogant disbelievers of Makkah.

5. Establishment of the principle that whoever initiates an evil practice bears its burden and the burden of those who act upon it, as in the authentic Hadith.

3. Condemnation of hypocrisy and the disbelief of hypocrites, even if they claim to be believers, for they are not believers.

4. Description of the extreme disbelief and tyranny of the arrogant disbelievers of Makkah.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 29, verses 14–15:

Explanation of the words:

"And We certainly sent Noah": that is, Noah son of Lamakh, son of Matushalakh, son of Idris, from the offspring of Shayth (Seth) son of Adam. Between him and Adam there were a thousand years.

"So he remained among them a thousand years less fifty years": that is, he remained among them calling them to Allah, the Exalted, for nine hundred and fifty years.

"Then the flood seized them": that is, the great water that surrounded them, rose over them and drowned them.

"While they were wrongdoers": that is, polytheists.

"And We made it a sign for the worlds": that is, a lesson for people, that they may take heed from it and not associate partners with Allah or disobey.

Meaning of the two verses:

When Allah mentioned what His Messenger and the believers encountered from the polytheists of Quraysh, He mentioned Noah and Abraham, both of whom endured and suffered what Muhammad ﷺ and his companions had not suffered, so that this would be a consolation and a relief for them. Allah said: ﴿And We certainly sent Noah to his people﴾. The people of Noah at that time were all of mankind, since there was no one else. ﴿So he remained among them﴾, that is, he stayed calling them to the worship of Allah and to affirming His oneness, and to abandoning the five idols that they had, which were Wadd, Suwa', Yaghuth, Ya'uq and Nasr. These five were righteous men; when they died, they built over their graves and set up their images, on the pretext that these would remind them of Allah so that they would be eager for obedience and righteous deeds. Then Satan adorned for them their worship, so they worshipped them. Allah sent Noah to them as a messenger, and he called them to worship Allah and to abandon the worship of these. ﴿So he remained among them a thousand years less fifty years﴾, calling them, but they did not respond to him. ﴿So he prayed to his Lord: "I am overcome, so give victory"﴾ [al-Qamar: 10]. Allah answered him, saved him and the people of the ship, who were the believers, and the wife and son of Noah, Kan'an, perished in the flood, as did all mankind except Noah and those with him in the ship. They were about eighty souls. Noah left three sons: Sam, who is the father of the Arabs, Persians and Romans, and they are the Semitic race; Ham, who is the father of the Copts, the Sudanese and the Berbers; and Yafith, who is the father of the Turks, the Slavs, Gog and Magog. This is the meaning of His words: ﴿Then the flood seized them while they were wrongdoers﴾, that is, wronging themselves through association. ﴿So We saved him and the companions of the ship﴾, and among those in it were his three sons Sam, Ham and Yafith, and from them the earth was populated with people in the east, west, north and south. His words ﴿And We made it a sign for the worlds﴾ mean: the event of the flood and the ship from it, and his remaining for that long period with few responders. ﴿A sign﴾, that is, a lesson, ﴿for the worlds﴾, that is, for people, that they may take heed from it and not disobey their messengers or associate partners with their Lord. This applies if they take heed, and few take heed.

Guidance from the two verses:

From the guidance of the two verses:

1- The demonstration of Allah's way of sending messengers to guide creation.

2- The demonstration of how few responded to Noah despite the long period, which serves as consolation for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the callers to truth after him.

3- The demonstration of Allah destroying the wrongdoers and saving the believers, which is a lesson for those who take heed.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 29, verses 16–18:

Explanation of the words:

wa-Ibrahim (and Ibrahim): i.e., "and mention Ibrahim," according to the reading in the accusative (naṣb) for Ibrahim; and according to the reading in the nominative (raf'): "and among the messengers is Ibrahim."

u'budu Allah wa-ttaquhu (worship Allah and fear Him): i.e., believe in Him, make Him one in worship, and beware of associating anything with Him and disobeying Him.

awthanan (idols): idols, stones, images and statues.

wa-takhluqna ifkan (and you fabricate a lie): i.e., you invent falsehood, saying of the idols and images that they are gods, and you worship them.

fa-btaghu 'inda Allah al-rizq (so seek provision from Allah): i.e., seek provision from Allah, the Creator, the All-Knowing, not from idols and statues, which are carved and shaped by men's hands with chisels and axes.

wa-u'budu-hu (and worship Him): i.e., by believing in Him and making Him one, and thank Him by obeying Him.

wa-in tukadhdhibu (and if you deny): i.e., O people of Mecca, after this which We have presented to you of signs and lessons, then indeed nations before you denied.

wa-ma 'ala al-rasul (and the Messenger is not [responsible] except): i.e., Muhammad (ﷺ).

illa al-balagh al-mubin (except clear conveyance): he has conveyed and made clear, so his duty is discharged, and you are the deniers, upon whom the vengeance of Allah will soon descend.

Meaning of the verses:

This narrative is linked to the story of Nuh, to console the Messenger (ﷺ) and the believers, and to remind the Quraysh that in their persistence in polytheism and denial of the Messenger (ﷺ) they are heading toward what the deniers before them came to, unless they repent to Allah, return to Him in faith, obedience, and abandoning polytheism and sins. Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿And Ibrahim﴾, i.e., mention, O Our Messenger, Ibrahim, Our friend (khalil), ﴿when he said to his people﴾, the Babylonians, among whom was his father Azar, ﴿O my people, worship Allah﴾, i.e., by making Him one in worship, ﴿and fear Him﴾ by abandoning polytheism and disobedience, or else His punishment will befall you and His torment will descend upon you. His saying ﴿That is better for you﴾, i.e., faith, monotheism and obedience are better for you than disbelief, polytheism and disobedience, because the first brings good and the second brings evil, ﴿if you knew﴾ good and evil and could distinguish between them.

His saying, peace be upon him, ﴿You only worship, besides Allah, idols and fabricate a lie﴾: he informs them, making them aware of their error, saying ﴿You only worship, besides Allah, idols﴾, i.e., statues and images. Worship of idols and images is vain worship that brings you no benefit and repels from you no harm. Rather, He who must be worshipped is Allah, the Creator, the Provider, the Harmful and the Beneficent, the Giver of life and the Causer of death, the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing. As for idols, there is nothing in worshipping them except error and following desire. His saying to them ﴿and you fabricate a lie﴾, i.e., you make up falsehood by fabrication when you say of the images and idols that they are gods. His saying, peace be upon him, to his people ﴿Indeed, those whom you worship besides Allah do not possess for you any provision﴾: he, peace be upon him, informs them, making known to them a reality of which they are heedless, namely that those whom they worship besides Allah do not possess provision for them, because they are not able to do that. So what is the benefit then of worshipping them, and what need impels to it, if not heedlessness and ignorance? When he had refuted for them the worship of idols, he guided them to the worship of the One, the Subduer, so he said ﴿So seek provision from Allah﴾, if you have worshipped idols for that purpose, for Allah is the Provider, the Possessor of strength, the Firm; so seek provision from Him, for He is its owner and capable of giving it. ﴿And worship Him﴾ by believing in Him, in His Messenger, and in His oneness, ﴿and be thankful to Him﴾ for He provides for you and preserves your provision for you. His saying ﴿To Him you will be returned﴾ reminds them of the cause of their heedlessness and the source of their ignorance, which is their disbelief in the Resurrection; so He informs them that they will return to Him, the Exalted, and not to other than Him.

Therefore, let them come to know Him and worship Him, seeking His pleasure and His honour for them on the day they meet Him. His saying, exalted is He, ﴿And if you deny﴾, i.e., O people of Mecca, Our Messenger and deny Our revelation and disbelieve in Our meeting, then you are not alone in that. ﴿Then nations before you have denied﴾: the people of Nuh, 'Ad, Pharaoh, the people of Ibrahim, the companions of Madyan and others. ﴿And upon the Messenger is only the clear conveyance﴾, i.e., Our Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) is only charged with clear conveyance, and he has conveyed to you, and you are now between two choices with no third: the first is that you take heed from what We have made you hear and shown you of Our signs, so that you believe, make Him one, and obey, and thus you will be perfected and made happy; and the other is that you persist in your polytheism, disbelief and disobedience, in which case there will befall you what befell the likes of you, for your disbelievers are no better than the disbelievers of those whom Allah punished and made them taste the evil of the torment. This is what verse [18] indicates, and it is an interjection between the verses which contained the story of Ibrahim, peace be upon him. The reason for the interjection is the presence of an opportunity in the context of speech which may catch the attention of the people and win their hearts, since all the verses are directed toward their guidance.

Guidance from the verses:

Among the guidance of the verses:

1- The obligation of worshipping Allah and fearing Him, seeking deliverance from loss in both abodes.

2- The invalidity of worshipping other than Allah, and the obligation of worshipping Allah by way of rational proofs.

3- People only worshipped idols out of their ignorance and poverty, so it is obligatory that they know that Allah is their Lord, deserving of their worship, and that Allah is the One who fills their need and provides for them, while whoever else does not possess that for them.

4- The obligation of thanking Allah, the Exalted, by praising Him and extolling Him, and by obeying Him and spending blessings on that for which He bestowed them upon His servant.

5- Consolation of the Messenger (ﷺ) and rebuke of the polytheists of Mecca.

**Explanation of the words:**

**Awa lam yaraw** (أولم يروا): that is, they should look with their eyes and thereby know with their hearts.

**Yubdi'u Allah al-khalq** (يبدئ الله الخلق): that is, how a creature is created from the beginning.

**Thumma yu'iduhu** (ثم يعيده): that is, then He, exalted is He, will bring it back after its beginning and its annihilation. He will restore it because restoration is easier than initiation. Since He has already originated and annihilated, He is necessarily able to restore.

**Inna dhalika** (إن ذلك): that is, the first creation and the second are the restoration.

He punishes those who disbelieve in Him and in His Messenger, and those who have not purified their souls through faith and righteous deeds, sending them to Hell, the abode of misery and torment. He shows mercy to the people of faith and piety, who have purified their souls through faith and righteous deeds.

His saying: ﴿And to Him you will be returned﴾, that is, to Allah your Lord you will return after death, annihilation, and the production of the final creation. His saying: ﴿And you cannot cause failure [to Him] within the earth or within the heaven﴾, that is, Allah, exalted is He. Rather, you are subdued to Him, submitting to His authority, and you cannot flee from Him or be freed from Him in any way. You have no protector other than Him who would take charge of you and repel the punishment from you, and no helper who would aid you, so that you would not be overcome or punished.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah﴾, which His messengers brought, ﴿and in His meeting﴾, which is the final resurrection that necessitates standing before Allah for questioning, reckoning, and recompense. This applies if the servant has good deeds for which he is called to account. But if he has no good deeds, he will be cast into Hell without reckoning or weighing, since he has no righteous deeds by which he could be weighed and called to account. Therefore He, exalted is He, says: ﴿Those﴾, that is, those who deny the signs of Allah and His meeting, ﴿have despaired of My mercy﴾, for their denial of the Qur'an prevents them from faith and righteous deeds, and their denial of the Day of Judgment prevents them from abandoning polytheism and sins, or from doing any righteous deed, because they deny recompense. So they despair of Paradise. ﴿And those will have a painful punishment﴾, that is, a painful torment, which is the punishment of the Fire in Hell, and we seek refuge in Allah, exalted is He.

**Guidance from the verses:**

1. The obligation to use reason to infer the unseen from the seen and the non-existent from the existent.
2. The affirmation of the belief in the resurrection and recompense, and the mention of its detailed evidences.
3. The affirmation of man's complete helplessness, and that he has no escape from Allah, his Lord and Owner. This condition calls for fleeing to Allah today through faith and piety.
4. A warning to the deniers that if they die in denial of the resurrection, they will never enter Paradise, and they will be punished in the Fire of Hell with the most severe punishment.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 29, verses 24–25:

Explanation of the words:

﴿فَما كانَ جَوابَ قَوْمِهِ﴾ (So was not the answer of his people): i.e., the people of Ibrahim (peace be upon him).

﴿إلاَّ أن قالُواْ ٱقْتُلُوهُ أوْ حَرِّقُوهُ﴾ (except that they said, "Kill him or burn him"): i.e., except their saying "Kill him" or "Burn him."

﴿إن في ذلك لآيات﴾ (Indeed, in that are signs): i.e., in the fact that the fire did not burn the Friend (al-Khalil) and he came out from it unharmed.

﴿لقوم يؤمنون﴾ (for a people who believe): because the believers are the ones who benefit from the signs, for the life of their hearts.

﴿أوثاناً مودة بينكم﴾ (idols as a bond of affection among you): i.e., you have taken your idols as gods, befriending one another for the sake of worshipping them and loving one another because of that.

﴿في الحياة الدنيا﴾ (in the life of this world): i.e., this mutual affection and love over the gods is only in the life of this world, but not in the Hereafter.

﴿يكفر بعضكم ببعض﴾ (some of you will disown others): i.e., the leaders will disown their followers and disassociate themselves from them.

﴿ويلعن بعضكم بعضاً﴾ (and some of you will curse others): the followers will curse the leaders who led them into falsehood.

The meaning of the verses:

The context continues with the story of Ibrahim, the Friend (al-Khalil), peace be upon him. When he silenced them with proof, made their falsehood clear to them, and exposed their ignorance and misguidance, they resorted, as is the custom of tyrants among the people of disbelief and falsehood, to threatening with force. So Allah, the Exalted, related what they said: ﴿فَما كانَ جَوابَ قَوْمِهِ﴾ — that is, the answer of his people, i.e., their response to the proofs and evidences they heard against polytheism and for the soundness of monotheism, was ﴿إلاَّ أن قالُواْ ٱقْتُلُوهُ أوْ حَرِّقُوهُ﴾ — except their saying: kill Ibrahim with the sword or the like, or burn him with fire. They carried out their crime in deed, kindled the fire, and threw him into it. Allah, majestic is His majesty, said to the fire: ﴿يٰنارُ كُونِي بَرْداً وسَلَٰماً عَلىٰ إبْراهِيمَ﴾ [al-Anbiya: 69], so it became as it was commanded, and Ibrahim came out unharmed; the fire burned nothing except the bonds with which his hands and feet were tied. This is what is indicated by His saying: ﴿فَأَنْجاهُ ٱللَّهُ مِنَ ٱلنّارِ﴾ and His saying: ﴿إنَّ فِي ذٰلِكَ لآياتٍ لِّقَوْمٍ يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ — i.e., in the fact that the fire did not burn Ibrahim, so its nature was changed and it became coolness and safety upon Ibrahim, and it did not burn him. (Signs) means evidences of Allah's power, mercy, and wisdom. But those signs benefit only the believers, because the others are dead: they do not hear, see, or understand. As for the believers, they are alive, so they benefit from what they hear and see, because faith is like the spirit in the body; if it is found in the heart, the body is alive, and if it departs from it, the body is dead, so neither does the eye see the events nor does the ear hear the signs.

As for His saying: ﴿إنَّما ٱتَّخَذْتُمْ مِّن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ أوْثاناً مَّوَدَّةَ بَيْنِكُمْ فِي ٱلْحَياةِ ٱلدُّنْيا﴾ — this is part of Ibrahim's speech to his people as he admonishes and guides them. He informed them of a reality they ignore, namely that they did not take those idols as gods to worship except for the sake of mutual acquaintance, affection, and love for their sake: they hold festivals for them, gather around them, and eat and drink, not because they truly believe they are gods, while they are stones they carved with their own hands and set up as statues in the courtyards of their houses and in front of their dwellings. And ﴿يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيامَةِ﴾ — that is, in the Hereafter, the opposite of this will happen to them, as ﴿يَكْفُرُ بَعْضُكُمْ بِبَعْضٍ ويَلْعَنُ بَعْضُكُمْ بَعْضاً﴾ — i.e., the ones who were followed, the leaders, will disown those who followed them, the common masses and ordinary people. ﴿ويَلْعَنُ بَعْضُكُمْ بَعْضاً﴾ — each of the followers and the followed will seek to distance himself from the other and deny him, at the moment of witnessing the punishment, and those ties and connections they had in this life will no longer remain!! And His saying: ﴿ومَأْواكُمُ ٱلنّارُ﴾ — i.e., your abode that shelters you all, where you will settle, is the Fire, ﴿وما لَكُمْ مِّن نّاصِرِينَ﴾ — and you will have no helpers after Allah has humiliated you, the One to whom you associated idols, making them a bond of affection among you in the life of this world.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- Establishing that it is the way of wrongdoers that when proofs fail them, they resort to the use of force.

2- The fire not burning him is evidence that Allah, the Exalted, is able to nullify customary laws when He wills, and from here arise the karamat (divine marvels granted to saints) and the miracles, which are departures from ordinary custom.

3- Clarification that those given to superstition, in gathering together upon innovations, do not do so out of knowledge of the benefit of the innovation, but only for the element of mutual affection, acquaintance, and gathering to eat and drink, as Ibrahim said to his people: ﴿إنَّما ٱتَّخَذْتُمْ مِّن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ أوْثاناً مَّوَدَّةَ بَيْنِكُمْ فِي ٱلْحَياةِ ٱلدُّنْيا﴾.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 29, verses 26–27:

Explanation of the words:

"فآمن له لوط" (So Lut believed in him): that is, he believed in Ibrahim. Lut was the son of his brother Haran, and no one from his people believed in him except Lut.

"مهاجر إلى ربي" (I will emigrate to my Lord): that is, to wherever I may worship my Lord without being tested in my religion.

"ووهبنا له إسحاق ويعقوب" (And We gave him Ishaq and Ya'qub): that is, he emigrated for Our sake, so We honoured him in the land of his emigration and granted him offspring: Ishaq, the son, and Ya'qub, the grandson.

"في ذريته النبوة والكتاب" (And among his descendants We placed prophethood and the Book): so all the prophets after him were from his descendants, and all the books revealed after him are among his descendants.

"وآتيناه أجره في الدنيا" (And We gave him his reward in this world): this was through good provision and a good reputation on the tongues of all people from the divine religions.

"وإنه في الآخرة لمن الصالحين" (And indeed, in the Hereafter he is among the righteous): that is, he is one of them, so he is honoured as they are honoured, with the highest ranks. The righteous are the prophets and messengers of God, His friends, and the righteous among His servants.

Meaning of the verses:

This is the end of the story of Ibrahim the Friend (al-Khalil) in this noble context. God informs that Ibrahim, after a long struggle in calling to the worship of the Most Merciful, was not believed in and was not followed in the truth he called to, except by Lut, son of Haran, his brother. God said: ﴿So Lut believed in him﴾, and [Ibrahim] said, that is, ﴿Indeed, I am emigrating to my Lord﴾, so he left the lands of his people in the fertile plain of Iraq and travelled to the land of Sham. God honoured him, as a reward for his emigration to his Lord, the Mighty and Wise, with what He mentions in this context, saying: ﴿And We gave him Ishaq and Ya'qub, and placed in his descendants prophethood and the Book﴾. "Gave him" means He bestowed upon him: his son Ishaq, son of Sarah, and Ishaq's son, Ya'qub. He placed all the prophets among his descendants, and also placed the Book among them: the Torah was revealed to Musa, the Psalms to Dawud, and the Gospel to Isa, and they are all from the descendants of Ibrahim; and the noble Qur'an was revealed to Muhammad (ﷺ), who is from the descendants of Isma'il son of Ibrahim. Ibrahim's statement was as he said: ﴿Indeed, I am emigrating to my Lord﴾, and he described his Lord with might and wisdom, so He said: ﴿Indeed, He is the Mighty, the Wise﴾, that is, the Overpowering, the Subduer; ﴿the Wise﴾ who places everything in its proper place. Among the signs of His might is that He saved Ibrahim from the hands of the oppressive tyrants, and among the manifestations of His wisdom is that He moved him from a land with no good in it to a land full of good, and honoured him there with what is mentioned in His words: ﴿And We gave him Ishaq and Ya'qub, and placed in his descendants prophethood and the Book﴾, and His words, the Exalted: ﴿And We gave him his reward in this world﴾, where He provided him with the finest provisions in the land of his emigration and granted him a good reputation from all the people of the divine religions, such as Judaism, Christianity, and Islam, which is the seal of the religions. This is in this world; as for the Hereafter, he is among the righteous, possessing the high ranks and lofty stations in the processions of the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs, and the righteous.

Guidance of the verses:

Among the guidance of these verses:

1- Explanation of the outcome of Ibrahim's call, that it was only believed by one person, Lut, peace be upon him, and in this there is consolation for the Noble Messenger (ﷺ).

2- Explanation of God's honouring of whoever emigrates to Him and leaves his family and home.

3- Explanation of what God honoured Ibrahim with of the good of this world and the Hereafter, as a reward for his patience in calling to God.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 29, verses 28–30:

Explanation of the words:

﴿وَلُوطًا إِذْ قَالَ لِقَوْمِهِ﴾ (And Lot, when he said to his people): i.e., and remember when Lot, son of Haran, said to his people, the people of Sodom.

﴿أَئِنَّكُمْ لَتَأْتُونَ الْفَاحِشَةَ﴾ (Do you really commit the abomination): i.e., the ugly deed, namely sexual intercourse with males in their anuses.

﴿مَا سَبَقَكُم بِهَا مِنْ أَحَدٍ مِّنَ الْعَالَمِينَ﴾ (No one in all the worlds had committed it before you): i.e., mankind did not know sexual intercourse with males in their anuses before the people of Lot.

﴿وَتَقْطَعُونَ السَّبِيلَ﴾ (And you cut off the road): i.e., by attacking passersby on the road, so that people refrained from passing through it out of fear of you.

﴿وَتَأْتُونَ فِي نَادِيكُمُ الْمُنكَرَ﴾ (And you commit wrongdoing in your gatherings): i.e., in the places where you converse you commit the wrong, such as passing wind openly, untying one's waistwrap, and the abomination, which is sodomy.

﴿فَمَا كَانَ جَوَابَ قَوْمِهِ﴾ (So the answer of his people was): i.e., nothing but their saying, "Bring us the punishment of God, if you are among the truthful."

Meaning of the verses:

This is the beginning of the account of Lot, peace be upon him, with his people, the people of Sodom and Amorah. The purpose of its context is to affirm the prophethood of Muhammad, since stories like these can only be known through revelation, and to console the Messenger for what he meets of the stubbornness of the polytheists and their demands for signs and punishment. God the Exalted said: Mention, O our Messenger, to your people Lot, ﴿And Lot, when he said to his people: "Do you really commit the abomination which no one in all the worlds has committed before you?"﴾ That is the ugly deed, and what makes it uglier is that this trait had not arisen among people before the people of Lot, and no one among the worlds had known it. Then Lot continued his denunciation and reproach of them, saying: ﴿"Do you really approach males, and cut off the road, and commit wrongdoing in your gatherings?"﴾ That is, in their anuses. ﴿And cut off the road﴾: they used to attack passersby, committing the abomination with them by force and robbing their wealth, so people refrained from passing and the road was cut off. Also, by their coupling with males they rendered offspring inoperative by cutting off the path of procreation. Lot increased his rebuke, censure and reproach of them, saying: ﴿"And you commit wrongdoing in your gatherings"﴾. The gathering is the place where they met and talked, and committing wrongdoing there was by perpetrating the abomination with one another, by passing wind openly, by untying waistwraps, by throwing pebbles, and what else is reported of them of evil and ugliness. God the Exalted said: ﴿So the answer of his people was﴾, after he had admonished and rebuked them, forbidding them from such abominations: ﴿nothing but that they said, "Bring us the punishment of God, if you are among the truthful."﴾ That is, their answer was nothing but a demand for the punishment of God. Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 29, verses 31–35:

Explanation of the words:

*bil-bushra* (with the glad tidings): namely Isaac, and Jacob after him.

*hadhihi al-qarya* (this town): namely the town of Lot, which is Sodom.

*qalu nahnu a'lamu bi-man fiha* (they said: "We know best who is in it"): that is, the messengers said: "We know best who is in it."

*kanat min al-ghabirin* (she was among those who remain behind): that is, she was, in Allah's knowledge and decree, among those who remain behind to be punished.

*sii'a bihim* (he was distressed on their account): that is, he was troubled and grieved, out of fear that his people would target them with harm.

*wa-daqa bihim dharʿan* (and he was straitened for them): that is, he was unable to bear the matter, fearing that his people would inflict harm on his guests.

*rijzan* (a punishment): that is, a punishment from the sky.

*bima kanu yafsuqun* (because of their wickedness): that is, because of their wickedness, which was committing the vile sin.

*wa-laqad taraknا minha ayatan* (and We have certainly left from it a sign): that is, We left, from the town of Sodom which We destroyed, a clear sign, which is its ruin and destruction and its transformation into a dead sea in which there is no life.

*li-qawmin yaʿqilun* (for a people who reason): that is, who know the causes and consequences when they reflect.

Explanation of the verses:

The discourse continues on the story of Lot, peace be upon him. After he warned them of Allah's punishment, they said, as is the habit of the deniers who are destroyed: "Bring us the punishment of Allah, if you are among the truthful." He, peace be upon him, sought victory over them from his Lord, the Exalted, and Allah answered him. This verse clarifies how that came about. The Exalted said: ﴿And when Our messengers came to Abraham﴾, the Friend, the paternal uncle of Lot, ﴿with the glad tidings﴾, which was the birth of a son to him, namely Isaac, and after him Jacob, the son of Isaac, peace be upon him, as the Exalted said: ﴿So We gave him good tidings of Isaac and, after Isaac, Jacob﴾ [Hud: 71]. ﴿They said﴾, that is, the angels said to Abraham: ﴿Indeed, we are going to destroy the people of this town﴾, meaning the town of Lot's people, which is Sodom, and they gave as the reason their saying: ﴿Indeed, its people have been wrongdoers﴾, that is, wronging themselves by engaging in sins and committing vile acts, and wronging others, since they cut off the road. Here Abraham said to them: ﴿Indeed, within it is Lot﴾, who is not among the wrongdoers but is one of Allah's righteous servants. The angels answered him, saying: ﴿We know best who is in it﴾, more than you, O Abraham. ﴿We will surely save him and his family﴾ from destruction ﴿except his wife; she was among those who remain behind﴾, and that was because of the length of her life; so she will be destroyed with them for her disbelief and her collusion with the wrongdoers.

As for the Exalted's words: ﴿And when Our messengers came to Lot﴾, that is, when the angels reached Lot, coming from Abraham from Palestine, ﴿he was distressed on their account and was straitened for them﴾, that is, he was displeased with them and was struck by grief and worry, out of fear that his people would harm them, while they were his guests who had descended upon him. When the angels saw that from him, they reassured him with what the Exalted had told them, in His saying: ﴿And they said: "Do not fear, nor grieve"﴾, that is, on our account, ﴿nor grieve﴾ over those who will be destroyed from your people along with your wrongdoing people. ﴿Indeed, we will save you﴾ from the punishment, you and your family, that is, your believing wife and your two daughters, ﴿except your wife﴾, that is, the wrongdoing old woman, ﴿for she is among those who remain behind﴾, those whose lives were prolonged, and she will be destroyed with those who are destroyed.

As for the Exalted's words in verse [34]: ﴿Indeed, We are sending down upon the people of this town a punishment from the sky because of their wickedness﴾, that is, the angels informed Lot of what they were going to do to his people, which is their saying: ﴿Indeed, We are sending down upon the people of this town﴾, that is, the city of Sodom, ﴿a punishment﴾, that is, a punishment from the sky, which was stones, ﴿because of their wickedness in committing the vile sin which no one among the worlds had preceded them in.

The Exalted said: ﴿And We have certainly left from it﴾, that is, from that town, ﴿a clear sign﴾, that is, a lesson and an example, and a manifest indication of Our power to destroy the wrongdoers and the corrupt. As for the Exalted's words: ﴿for a people who reason﴾, since they are the ones who reflect upon matters and draw out their causes, factors, consequences and effects. As for those who do not reason, they have no share or portion in that; they are like the cattle led to the slaughterhouse, not knowing. In this there is an allusion to the polytheists of Mecca and their foolishness and heedlessness.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- The forbearance and mercy of Abraham, manifested in his defense of Lot and his family.

2- Establishing the principle: "Whoever is held back by his deeds will not be advanced by his lineage." Lot's marital bond with his old wife did not benefit her, and she was destroyed because she was with the wrongdoers in her heart and conduct.

3- The legitimacy of hospitality and its emphasis in Islam, due to the sahih hadith: "Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him honor his guest." 4- Condemnation of wickedness against the obedience of Allah, which is the cause of the destruction of nations and peoples.

5- The virtue of reason when its possessor uses it to recognize truth and falsehood, good and evil.

*qalu nahnu a'lamu bi-man fiha* (they said: "We know best who is in it"): that is, the messengers said: "We know best who is in it."

*kanat min al-ghabirin* (she was among those who remain behind): that is, she was, in Allah's knowledge and decree, among those who remain behind to be punished.

*sii'a bihim* (he was distressed on their account): that is, he was troubled and grieved, out of fear that his people would target them with harm.

*wa-daqa bihim dharʿan* (and he was straitened for them): that is, he was unable to bear the matter, fearing that his people would inflict harm on his guests.

*rijzan* (a punishment): that is, a punishment from the sky.

*bima kanu yafsuqun* (because of their wickedness): that is, because of their wickedness, which was committing the vile sin.

*wa-laqad taraknا minha ayatan* (and We have certainly left from it a sign): that is, We left, from the town of Sodom which We destroyed, a clear sign, which is its ruin and destruction and its transformation into a dead sea in which there is no life.

*li-qawmin yaʿqilun* (for a people who reason): that is, who know the causes and consequences when they reflect.

Explanation of the verses:

The discourse continues on the story of Lot, peace be upon him. After he warned them of Allah's punishment, they said, as is the habit of the deniers who are destroyed: "Bring us the punishment of Allah, if you are among the truthful." He, peace be upon him, sought victory over them from his Lord, the Exalted, and Allah answered him. This verse clarifies how that came about. The Exalted said: ﴿And when Our messengers came to Abraham﴾, the Friend, the paternal uncle of Lot, ﴿with the glad tidings﴾, which was the birth of a son to him, namely Isaac, and after him Jacob, the son of Isaac, peace be upon him, as the Exalted said: ﴿So We gave him good tidings of Isaac and, after Isaac, Jacob﴾ [Hud: 71]. ﴿They said﴾, that is, the angels said to Abraham: ﴿Indeed, we are going to destroy the people of this town﴾, meaning the town of Lot's people, which is Sodom, and they gave as the reason their saying: ﴿Indeed, its people have been wrongdoers﴾, that is, wronging themselves by engaging in sins and committing vile acts, and wronging others, since they cut off the road. Here Abraham said to them: ﴿Indeed, within it is Lot﴾, who is not among the wrongdoers but is one of Allah's righteous servants. The angels answered him, saying: ﴿We know best who is in it﴾, more than you, O Abraham. ﴿We will surely save him and his family﴾ from destruction ﴿except his wife; she was among those who remain behind﴾, and that was because of the length of her life; so she will be destroyed with them for her disbelief and her collusion with the wrongdoers.

As for the Exalted's words: ﴿And when Our messengers came to Lot﴾, that is, when the angels reached Lot, coming from Abraham from Palestine, ﴿he was distressed on their account and was straitened for them﴾, that is, he was displeased with them and was struck by grief and worry, out of fear that his people would harm them, while they were his guests who had descended upon him. When the angels saw that from him, they reassured him with what the Exalted had told them, in His saying: ﴿And they said: "Do not fear, nor grieve"﴾, that is, on our account, ﴿nor grieve﴾ over those who will be destroyed from your people along with your wrongdoing people. ﴿Indeed, we will save you﴾ from the punishment, you and your family, that is, your believing wife and your two daughters, ﴿except your wife﴾, that is, the wrongdoing old woman, ﴿for she is among those who remain behind﴾, those whose lives were prolonged, and she will be destroyed with those who are destroyed.

As for the Exalted's words in verse [34]: ﴿Indeed, We are sending down upon the people of this town a punishment from the sky because of their wickedness﴾, that is, the angels informed Lot of what they were going to do to his people, which is their saying: ﴿Indeed, We are sending down upon the people of this town﴾, that is, the city of Sodom, ﴿a punishment﴾, that is, a punishment from the sky, which was stones, ﴿because of their wickedness in committing the vile sin which no one among the worlds had preceded them in.

The Exalted said: ﴿And We have certainly left from it﴾, that is, from that town, ﴿a clear sign﴾, that is, a lesson and an example, and a manifest indication of Our power to destroy the wrongdoers and the corrupt. As for the Exalted's words: ﴿for a people who reason﴾, since they are the ones who reflect upon matters and draw out their causes, factors, consequences and effects. As for those who do not reason, they have no share or portion in that; they are like the cattle led to the slaughterhouse, not knowing. In this there is an allusion to the polytheists of Mecca and their foolishness and heedlessness.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- The forbearance and mercy of Abraham, manifested in his defense of Lot and his family.

2- Establishing the principle: "Whoever is held back by his deeds will not be advanced by his lineage." Lot's marital bond with his old wife did not benefit her, and she was destroyed because she was with the wrongdoers in her heart and conduct.

3- The legitimacy of hospitality and its emphasis in Islam, due to the sahih hadith: "Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him honor his guest." 4- Condemnation of wickedness against the obedience of Allah, which is the cause of the destruction of nations and peoples.

5- The virtue of reason when its possessor uses it to recognize truth and falsehood, good and evil.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 29, verses 36–37:

Explanation of the words:

*Wa ila Madyan* (And to Madyan): That is, We sent to the tribe of Madyan. Madyan was the forefather of the tribe, and so it was named after him.

*Akhahum Shu'ayban* (their brother Shu'ayb): That is, their brother by lineage.

*U'budu Allah* (Worship Allah): That is, worship Him alone and do not associate anything with Him.

*Warjou al-yawm al-akhir* (and hope for the Last Day): That is, believe in it, expect its coming, and [be mindful of] what will happen in it.

*Wa la ta'thaw fi al-ard mufsidin* (and do not commit corruption on the earth, causing corruption): That is, do not spread corruption on the earth, which is acting in acts of disobedience there.

*Fa-akhadhathum al-rajfah* (so the earthquake seized them): a violent shaking and a severe quake.

*Fi darihim jathimin* (lying prostrate in their homes): clinging to the ground, dead and motionless.

The meaning of the two verses:

This is a summary of the story of Shu'ayb, peace be upon him, with his people, the people of Madyan. The lesson from it is the destruction of that nation because it denied its messenger and persisted in polytheism and disobedience, so that the Quraysh might take heed from what befell this nation of ruin and devastation, because of their denial of their messenger and their disobedience to their Lord. God, Exalted, said: ﴿And to Madyan﴾, that is, And We sent to Madyan ﴿their brother Shu'ayb﴾, and he was an Arab prophet. When he reached them with his message, he said ﴿O my people, worship Allah﴾, that is, make Him one in worship and obey Him in what He commands you and forbids you, such as cheating in measure and weight, ﴿and hope for the Last Day﴾, that is, believe in the Day of Resurrection, always expect its coming, and fear what it contains of terrors and conditions, for that helps you toward righteousness. And His saying: ﴿And do not commit corruption on the earth, causing corruption﴾, because they diminished measure and weight, defrauded people of their goods, and spread corruption on the earth through acts of disobedience. And His saying, Exalted: ﴿But they denied him﴾, that is, the people of Madyan denied their prophet Shu'ayb in what he told them and called them to, ﴿so the earthquake seized them﴾, that is, the quake of destruction from beneath them, and they became in their homes lying prostrate on their knees, dead. God did not wrong them, but they were the wrongdoers.

Guidance from the two verses:

From the guidance of the two verses:

1. Affirmation of monotheism, prophethood, and the Final Resurrection.

2. The prohibition of corruption on the earth, by committing acts of disobedience and engaging in sins.

3. Demonstration of God's retribution against those who deny, wrong, and transgress.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 29, verses 38–40:

Explanation of the words:

﴿وعاداً وثمودا﴾: That is, We destroyed the tribe of ʿAd and the tribe of Thamud likewise.

﴿وقد تبين لكم من مساكنهم﴾: That is, the destruction of them has become clear to you from their dwellings, which lie empty of them, at al-Hijr in the north of the Hijaz and al-Shihr in the south of Yemen.

﴿عن السبيل﴾: That is, the path of guidance and truth which their messengers had made clear to them.

﴿كانوا مستبصرين﴾: That is, possessors of insight, since their messengers had taught them.

﴿وقارون وفرعون وهامان﴾: That is, We destroyed Qarun by being swallowed up by the earth, and Pharaoh and Haman by drowning.

﴿فاستكبروا﴾: That is, they were arrogant toward the worship of God Most High, obedience to Him, and obedience to His messengers.

﴿وما كانوا سابقين﴾: That is, they were not escaping the punishment of God, meaning they could not flee from it; rather it overtook them.

﴿فكلاً أخذنا بذنبه﴾: That is, each one of those mentioned We seized for his sin, and none of them escaped from Us.

﴿ومنهم من أرسلنا عليه حاصباً﴾: That is, a violent wind, as with ʿAd.

﴿ومنهم من أخذته الصيحة﴾: That is, Thamud.

﴿ومنهم من خسفنا به الأرض﴾: That is, like Qarun.

﴿ومنهم من أغرقنا﴾: Like the people of Noah and Pharaoh.

Meaning of the verses:

When God Most High mentioned in the preceding verses the destruction of the people of Lot, the people of Shuʿayb and the people of Noah, who rejected His call and denied His messengers, He mentioned the rest of the peoples who denied the signs of God and His messengers, and destroyed them. He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿وعاداً وثَمُوداْ﴾, that is, We likewise destroyed ʿAd, the people of Hud, and Thamud, the people of Salih. And His saying: ﴿وقَد تَّبَيَّنَ لَكُم مِّن مَّساكِنِهِمْ﴾, that is, it has become clear to you, O company of the disbelievers of Makkah and the polytheists of Quraysh, from their dwellings at al-Hijr and al-Shihr of Hadramawt, what confirms to you Our destruction of them, for their desolate dwellings are a clear proof of that, a proof by direct observation. And His saying: ﴿وزَيَّنَ لَهُمُ ٱلشَّيْطانُ أعْمالَهُمْ﴾, that is, Satan adorned for them their deeds of polytheism, evil, wrongdoing and corruption, and by this adornment he turned them away from the path, the path of faith and piety that brings happiness in this world and the Hereafter. And His saying: ﴿وكانُواْ مُسْتَبْصِرِينَ﴾, that is, possessors of insight, meaning knowledge of truth and falsehood, good and evil, which the messengers had taught them, but they preferred their desires over their intellects, and so they perished. God did not wrong them, but they were the wrongdoers. And His saying: ﴿وقارُونَ وفِرْعَوْنَ وهامانَ﴾, that is, We destroyed Qarun the Israelite, the cousin of Moses, peace be upon him, We destroyed him for his rebellion and disbelief, so We caused the earth to swallow him and his house as well; and Pharaoh and Haman, We drowned them in the sea for their disbelief, their transgression, their wrongdoing and their arrogance, and that was after Moses had brought them the clear signs and the evident proofs, which left them no excuse for refraining from faith and piety. But ﴿فَٱسْتَكْبَرُواْ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ﴾, in the land of Egypt and its territories, so they rejected faith and piety, ﴿وما كانُواْ سابِقِينَ﴾, nor were they escaping; so God Most High brought down upon them His vengeance and sent upon them His might, which cannot be turned back from the wrongdoing people. Then in the fortieth verse of this passage, God Most High explained the kinds of punishment by which these peoples were destroyed, and He said: ﴿فَكُلاًّ﴾, that is, each one of these deniers ﴿أخَذْنا بِذَنبِهِ فَمِنهُم مَّن أرْسَلْنا عَلَيْهِ حاصِباً﴾, that is, a violent wind, as with ʿAd. ﴿ومِنهُمْ مَّنْ أخَذَتْهُ ٱلصَّيْحَةُ﴾, as with Thamud. ﴿ومِنهُمْ مَّنْ خَسَفْنا بِهِ ٱلأَرْضَ﴾, as with Qarun. ﴿ومِنهُمْ مَّنْ أغْرَقْنا﴾, as with Pharaoh. And His saying: ﴿وما كانَ ٱللَّهُ لِيَظْلِمَهُمْ﴾, that is, it is not in the nature of God Most High to do wrong so as to wrong them, ﴿ولَٰكِن كانُوۤاْ﴾, that is, those peoples, ﴿أنفُسَهُمْ يَظْلِمُونَ﴾, wronging themselves through polytheism, disbelief, denial and sins, and so they destroyed themselves by that, and they were the wrongdoers.

Guidance of the verses:

1- Clarification that Satan is the cause of the peoples' destruction, through his adorning for them of evil and ugliness such as polytheism, falsehood, wickedness and corruption.

2- Clarification that arrogance, like wrongdoing, has as its outcome destruction and loss.

3- Clarification that God Most High does not destroy a community until He has made clear to it what it must guard against of the causes of destruction and ruin; if it refuses except that, God brings it to the place where its path ends.

Guidance of the verses:

1- Clarification that Satan is the cause of the peoples' destruction, through his adorning for them of evil and ugliness such as polytheism, falsehood, wickedness and corruption.

2- Clarification that arrogance, like wrongdoing, has as its outcome destruction and loss.

**Explanation of the words:**

*"The likeness of those who take other than Allah as protectors"*: that is, the description and condition of those who take idols, hoping for their benefit.

*"Like the spider, which takes a house"*: that is, for itself, to shelter in.

*"The weakest of houses"*: the feeblest of houses and the least useful.

*"Allah knows what they call upon besides Him of anything"*: that is, of the idols, images and others.

*"And He is the Mighty, the Wise"*: that is, the One who prevails over His affair, the Wise in managing the affairs of His creation.

*"And none understands them except the knowing"*: that is, those who know Allah, His signs, the rulings of His law and its secrets.

*"Allah created the heavens and the earth with truth"*: that is, so that He may be worshipped, not in play and not in falsehood.

*"Recite what has been revealed to you of the Book"*: O Messenger, recite what has been sent down to you of the Qur'an.

*"And establish the prayer"*: by performing it in its proper standing, observing its conditions, pillars, obligatory parts and recommended parts.

*"It forbids immorality and wrongdoing"*: that is, the prayer, through the light it produces in the heart of the servant, so that he becomes unable to commit an indecency or commit an evil.

*"And the remembrance of Allah is greater"*: that is, Allah's remembrance of His servant is greater than the servant's remembrance of his Lord, just as the remembrance of Allah is greater in forbidding immorality and wrongdoing than the prayer and other acts.

**Meaning of the verses:**

After the Exalted mentioned His punishment of His enemies who disbelieved in Him, associated others with Him in worship, and denied His messengers, this was a warning and instruction for the polytheists and disbelievers contemporary with the revelation of the Qur'an, so that perhaps they would respond to the Muhammadan call, believe, affirm the oneness of God, submit, and be saved from punishment and loss. Here, in these verses, He mentions an example of worshipping idols and their uselessness to their worshippers. The aim is to establish monotheism (*tawhid*) and to nullify shirk, which prevents human perfection and happiness.

The Exalted said: *"The likeness of those who take other than Allah"*, that is, partners, which are idols and images, which they worship hoping for their benefit and their intercession for them with Allah the Exalted. *"Like the spider, which takes a house"*, to shelter in, seeking protection from what it fears, such as cold or an insect's assault on it. *"And indeed, the weakest of houses is the spider's house"*, while the weakest of houses, that is, the feeblest, lowliest and least protective, is the spider's house. Such is the condition of the polytheists who take *"protectors"* other than Allah, that is, idols, hoping for benefit and for the repelling of harm through them. They are deluded in this, mistaken and erring. Indeed, none benefits or harms except Allah, so let them worship Him alone and abandon what is other than Him.

His saying: *"If only they knew"*, that is, if the polytheists knew that their condition in worshipping other than Allah, in gaining no benefit from it, is like the spider's condition in gaining no benefit from its frail house, they would not have been content with worshipping other than Allah, and would have abandoned the worship of Allah, in whose hand is everything and to whom everything returns.

His saying: *"Indeed, Allah knows what they call upon besides Him of anything"* contains a threat to the polytheists who persist in shirk, that what they do of calling upon others is not hidden from Him. Had He willed, He would have destroyed them as He destroyed those before them. *"And He is the Mighty"*, that is, the One who prevails over His affair, *"the Wise"* in managing His creation. Therefore He hastens punishment for whom He hastens it, for a wisdom, and postpones it for whom He postpones it, for a wisdom. So let the polytheists not be deceived by the delay of punishment, nor take it as evidence of Allah's approval of their worship. How could He approve of it when He destroyed nations for it, sent down His Book, and sent His Messenger to nullify it and eliminate it?

His saying: *"And these examples We present to the people"*, that is, these examples We present to people in order to awaken them, make them perceive, and guide them. *"And none understands them except the knowing"*, that is, none grasps their meaning and the purpose they aim at, which is to warn against shirk, the obstacle to every perfection and happiness in both abodes, *"except the knowing"*, that is, those who know Allah, His laws, the secrets of His speech and what His signs guide to.

His saying: *"Allah created the heavens and the earth with truth"* is a report that He, the Exalted, is the One who created the heavens and the earth. They are manifestations of His power, knowledge and wisdom, which necessitate worshipping Him through glorifying, obeying and loving Him, turning to Him in repentance (*inabah*), and fearing Him. They were created with truth, not with falsehood, and that is so that He may be remembered and thanked in them. Whoever disbelieves in Him and abandons His remembrance and thanks is like one who toys with the heavens and the earth and corrupts them. Therefore, considering the greatness of his crime, he is punished with a punishment that is lasting and eternal.

His saying: *"Indeed, in that is a sign for the believers"*, that is, in the creation of the heavens and the earth with truth is *"a sign"*, an evident indication of the existence of Allah, His power, knowledge and wisdom. These are the grounds of His divinity over all His servants. He is the true God, having no lord other than Him and no god besides Him. After this clarification and proof, no excuse remains for one who makes excuses.

On this basis, *"recite"*, O Messenger, *"what has been revealed to you of the Book"*, for instruction, admonition, worship and drawing near (to Allah). *"And establish the prayer"* at the two ends of the day and in the zulfa (nearer parts) of the night, for in that is great help for you in patience and steadfastness, and a great provision for your journey to the supreme malakut (the realm of the unseen dominion).

His saying: *"Indeed, the prayer forbids immorality and wrongdoing"* gives the reason for the command to establish the prayer. The prayer, through the illuminations it produces in the soul, heart and intellect, becomes a state that stands between the servant and being polluted with the filth of indecencies and the corruptions of wrongdoing. This indicates that what is meant is establishing the prayer, not merely performing it and carrying it out. Establishing the prayer is realized by sincerity in it to Allah the Exalted first; then by purifying the heart from turning to other than the Lord during its performance, second; then by performing it at its appointed times and in the mosques, the houses of Allah, and with the community of Muslims, the servants and friends of Allah; then by observing its pillars: the recitation of al-Fatiha, bowing (*ruku*) and tranquillity in it, rising (*i'tidal*) and tranquillity in it, and prostration upon the forehead and nose with tranquillity in it. The last of its pillars is *khushu'*, which is stillness, softness of the heart, and the shedding of tears. This is the prayer which produces the energy of light that prevents immersion in desires and sins, committing indecency and perpetrating wrongdoing.

His saying: *"And the remembrance of Allah is greater"*, that is, greater in forbidding immorality and wrongdoing than establishing the prayer, because the prayer, while being performed, is a preventive safeguard, but once one leaves it, its effect may weaken. As for the remembrance of Allah with the heart and tongue at all times, it is a safeguard preventing falling into immorality and wrongdoing. The phrase also carries another meaning: Allah's remembrance of the servant in the supreme malakut is greater than the servant's remembrance of the Lord in the malakut of the earth. This is indicated by His saying in the authentic hadith: "Whoever remembers Me within himself, I remember him within Myself; and whoever remembers Me in a gathering, I remember him in a gathering better than it." Certainly, by Allah, the Lord's remembrance of the weak servant is greater than the weak servant's remembrance of the mighty Lord. O Allah, make us among those who remember and thank You for Your blessings.

His saying: *"And Allah knows what you do"* contains both promise and warning, for His knowledge entails recompense. Whoever does good is rewarded for it, and whoever does evil is rewarded for it. O Allah, provide us with the doing of good and keep us far from the doing of evil. Amen.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 29, verse 46–49:

Explanation of the words:

﴿And do not argue with the People of the Book⦆: That is, do not debate or dispute with the Jews or the Christians.

﴿except in a way that is best⦆: That is, only with the argument that is best, which is calling to God through His signs and drawing attention to His proofs.

﴿except those of them who have wronged⦆: That is, those who did not enter into the protection (dhimmah) of the Muslims by paying the jizyah (poll tax) and remained at war with the Muslims.

﴿And thus We have sent down to you the Book⦆: That is, just as We sent down the Book to the messengers before you, We have sent down the Book to you.

﴿Those to whom We have given the Book believe in it⦆: That is, like 'Abd Allah ibn Salam and his brethren who believed in the Messenger and his Book.

﴿And among these there are those who believe in it⦆: That is, among these polytheists there are those who believe in it, and indeed many believed in it.

﴿And you did not recite before it any scripture, nor did you write it with your right hand⦆: That is, you did not write with your hand, because you are an unlettered (ummi) man who neither reads nor writes.

﴿Otherwise, the falsifiers would have had cause for doubt⦆: That is, the Jews would have doubted your prophethood and the descent of the Qur'an to you.

﴿Rather, it is clear signs in the breasts of those who have been given knowledge⦆: That is, the description and attributes of Muhammad ﷺ are clear signs in the Torah and the Gospel, preserved in the hearts of those among the People of the Book who have been given knowledge.

﴿And none reject Our signs except the wrongdoers⦆: That is, none reject the signs of God that carry the attributes and characteristics of the unlettered Messenger except those who have wronged themselves by concealing the truth and persisting in falsehood.

Meaning of the verses:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And do not argue with the People of the Book﴾. This is a teaching for the Messenger ﷺ and for the believers, who should act upon it in the future when they come into contact with and mix with the People of the Book. The Mighty and Majestic said, addressing the Messenger ﷺ and the believers of his community: ﴿And do not argue with the People of the Book﴾, who are the Jews and the Christians, forbidding them from disputing with them, which means contending, arguing and debating with them, ﴿except in a way that is best﴾, that is, except with the argument that is best, which is by calling them to God, the Exalted, so that they believe in His Messenger and enter His religion, Islam, and by drawing attention to the proofs of God and the evidences of His revelation and His Book. His words ﴿except those of them who have wronged﴾ refer to those who did not enter into the protection of the Muslims and did not pay the jizyah, and who took up war and hostility against the Muslims. Such people are not to be argued with; rather, the sword is applied to them, and they are fought until they give the jizyah willingly while they are humbled. His words, the Exalted: ﴿And say: "We believe in what has been revealed to us and what has been revealed to you; our God and your God is One, and to Him we are Muslims."﴾ This is another teaching for the believers, namely: if the People of the Book inform them of something which Islam neither confirms nor denies, and they claim that it is in their book, then say what God the Exalted has guided us to say, which is: ﴿We believe in what has been revealed to us﴾ to the end of the verse, so that we neither falsely denounce the truth nor believe in falsehood. In al-Bukhari it is related that the Prophet ﷺ said: "Do not believe the People of the Book, nor disbelieve them, but say: ﴿We believe in what has been revealed to us and what has been revealed to you; our God and your God is One, and to Him we are Muslims.﴾"

His words, the Exalted: ﴿And thus We have sent down to you the Book﴾, that is, just as We sent down the earlier books to earlier messengers such as Moses, David and Jesus, peace be upon them, We have sent down to you, O Muhammad, the Book, that is, the Qur'an. His words, the Exalted: ﴿Those to whom We have given the Book believe in it, and among these there are those who believe in it, and none reject Our signs except the disbelievers.﴾

This is a report of the unseen. Just as God, the Exalted, taught the believers how to conduct themselves with the People of the Book when they come into contact with them and live among them in Medina and elsewhere, He informed that those to whom the Book was given, namely the Torah and the Gospel, and who are the firmly grounded in knowledge, believe in it, that is, in the Qur'an. 'Abd Allah ibn Salam and many of the rabbis of the People of the Book did believe, and many of the polytheists also believed, and so the matter was as He had informed. His words, the Exalted: ﴿And none reject Our signs except the disbelievers﴾: as He said, none reject and deny the Qur'anic signs except a disbeliever whose soul is dark and corrupt. His words, the Exalted: ﴿And you did not recite before it any scripture, nor did you write it with your right hand﴾: as the Mighty and Majestic said, the Messenger of God ﷺ did not recite any scripture before the Qur'an, nor did he write any scripture with his right hand, because he was unlettered, neither reading nor writing. That is, had he been reading and writing before the Qur'an was revealed to him, the falsifiers would have had room to doubt the validity of the claim to Muhammad's prophethood and the descent of the Qur'an upon him. But he did not read any scripture before the Qur'an, nor did he write any script or book with his right hand, so the polytheists had no argument left to make at all. His words, the Exalted: ﴿Rather, it is clear signs in the breasts of those who have been given knowledge﴾: that is, rather the Messenger, his description, and his attributes, among them the attribute of being unlettered, are clear signs in the Torah and the Gospel, preserved in the hearts of those among the People of the Book who have been given knowledge. His words, the Exalted: ﴿And none reject Our signs﴾ in the Torah, the Gospel and the Qur'an ﴿except the wrongdoers﴾ against themselves: the materialistic Jews and Christians who eat and seek leadership at the expense of the truth, God forbid.

Guidance of the verses:

Among the guidance of these verses:

1) The legitimacy of arguing with People of the Book who are under protection (dhimmis) in the best manner.

2) The prohibition of questioning the People of the Book, based on his saying ﷺ: "Do not ask the People of the Book about anything, for they will not guide you, and they have gone astray; either you will deny the truth or you will believe in falsehood."

3) The prohibition of either believing or disbelieving the People of the Book when they report something, and the obligation to say: ﴿We believe in what has been revealed to us and what has been revealed to you; our God and your God is One, and to Him we are Muslims.﴾

4) The Qur'an's report of the unseen before it occurs, which then comes to pass as reported, and this is a sign that it is the revelation of God, the Exalted.

5) The affirmation of the attribute of unlettered-ness in the Prophet ﷺ as it is in the earlier scriptures.
