Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 29, verses 50–52:

Explanation of the words:

"Why has no sign been sent down upon him?": That is, the disbelievers of Quraysh said: "Why has no sign from his Lord been sent down upon Muhammad, like the she-camel of Salih or the staff of Musa?"

"Say: The signs are only with Allah": That is, say, O Our Messenger, the signs are with Allah; He sends them down whenever He wills.

"Is it not sufficient for them that We have sent down to you the Book?": That is, is it not sufficient for them, in what they ask for of signs, that We have sent the Book down to you?

"Indeed, in that is mercy and a reminder": That is, in the Qur'an is mercy and admonition for the believers, and it is better than the she-camel of Salih.

"And those who believed in falsehood": This refers to what is worshipped besides Allah.

"And disbelieved in Allah": This refers to the true God.

"It is those who are the losers": That is, because they exchanged disbelief for faith.

Meaning of the verses:

The context remains on establishing the prophethood of Muhammad. His saying, exalted is He: "And they say" (i.e., the people of Mecca), "Why has no sign been sent down upon him from his Lord?" That is, why has no sign been sent down upon Muhammad from his Lord, like the she-camel of Salih, the staff of Musa, or the table of Isa, since these are what they mean by "signs," i.e., miracles that break the normal course of nature. Allah said to His Messenger ﷺ: Say, O Our Messenger, to your people who demand signs as proof of the truth of your prophethood: Firstly, the signs you demand are with Allah and not with me; He sends them down whenever He wills and upon whomever He wills. Secondly, "I am only a clear warner": that is, my duty that I carry out is to warn the people of wrongdoing about the consequence of their wrong, which is the punishment of the Fire; therefore, there is no sense in demanding signs from me. Thirdly: is it not a sign for them that Allah has sent down His Book upon me? I recite it to you morning and evening. What greater sign is there than a Book from an unlettered man who neither reads nor writes, whose verses are recited, bearing guidance and light, and which at the same time is mercy and a reminder, that is, an admonition, for a people who believe? It is a established, enduring, lasting miracle, in which the believers find mercy and show mercy to one another, and find in it admonition, so they take heed by it. How different this is from a miracle that lasts an hour and then vanishes, like the table of Isa or the staff of Musa. Fourthly: the testimony of Allah to my messengership is sufficient; no other proof is sought for my prophethood and messengership, for my Lord has said to me: "Say: Allah is sufficient as a witness between me and you." My Lord, who knows what is in the heavens and the earth of every unseen thing, and among that is His knowledge that I am His Messenger, has testified to this by sending down this Book to me. Finally, after this explanation, Allah says: "And those who believed in falsehood" — which is the deification of creatures besides Allah — "and disbelieved in Allah" — in the lordship of the true God — "those are the losers" — distant in corruption of intellect and poor understanding — "they are the losers" in their state when they bought disbelief in exchange for faith and substituted misguidance for guidance.

This is what the three verses indicate, so let their recitation be repeated with deliberation and reflection.

Guidance of the verses:

Among the guidance of these verses:

1) Establishing the prophethood of Muhammad through conclusive proofs that cannot be refuted, which are four, as mentioned above.

2) Showing the greatest miracle proving the prophethood of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, which is the revelation of the noble Qur'an to him. Concerning this, he (ﷺ) said, as in al-Bukhari: "There is no prophet except that he was given what people believed in because of its like, but what I was given is a revelation that Allah revealed to me, so I hope to be the most numerous of them in followers on the Day of Resurrection."
3) The noble Qur'an is mercy and a reminder, that is, a lesson and admonition for those who believe in it and for those upon whom it was sent down.

4) Establishing the loss of the polytheists in both abodes, for their exchanging falsehood for truth, and we seek refuge in Allah, the Exalted.

The context remains on establishing the prophethood of Muhammad. His saying, exalted is He: "And they say" (i.e., the people of Mecca), "Why has no sign been sent down upon him from his Lord?" That is, why has no sign been sent down upon Muhammad from his Lord, like the she-camel of Salih, the staff of Musa, or the table of Isa, since these are what they mean by "signs," i.e., miracles that break the normal course of nature. Allah said to His Messenger ﷺ: Say, O Our Messenger, to your people who demand signs as proof of the truth of your prophethood: Firstly, the signs you demand are with Allah and not with me; He sends them down whenever He wills and upon whomever He wills. Secondly, "I am only a clear warner": that is, my duty that I carry out is to warn the people of wrongdoing about the consequence of their wrong, which is the punishment of the Fire; therefore, there is no sense in demanding signs from me. Thirdly: is it not a sign for them that Allah has sent down His Book upon me? I recite it to you morning and evening. What greater sign is there than a Book from an unlettered man who neither reads nor writes, whose verses are recited, bearing guidance and light, and which at the same time is mercy and a reminder, that is, an admonition, for a people who believe? It is a established, enduring, lasting miracle, in which the believers find mercy and show mercy to one another, and find in it admonition, so they take heed by it. How different this is from a miracle that lasts an hour and then vanishes, like the table of Isa or the staff of Musa. Fourthly: the testimony of Allah to my messengership is sufficient; no other proof is sought for my prophethood and messengership, for my Lord has said to me: "Say: Allah is sufficient as a witness between me and you." My Lord, who knows what is in the heavens and the earth of every unseen thing, and among that is His knowledge that I am His Messenger, has testified to this by sending down this Book to me. Finally, after this explanation, Allah says: "And those who believed in falsehood" — which is the deification of creatures besides Allah — "and disbelieved in Allah" — in the lordship of the true God — "those are the losers" — distant in corruption of intellect and poor understanding — "they are the losers" in their state when they bought disbelief in exchange for faith and substituted misguidance for guidance.

This is what the three verses indicate, so let their recitation be repeated with deliberation and reflection.

Guidance of the verses:

Among the guidance of these verses:

1) Establishing the prophethood of Muhammad through conclusive proofs that cannot be refuted, which are four, as mentioned above.

2) Showing the greatest miracle proving the prophethood of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, which is the revelation of the noble Qur'an to him. Concerning this, he (ﷺ) said, as in al-Bukhari: "There is no prophet except that he was given what people believed in because of its like, but what I was given is a revelation that Allah revealed to me, so I hope to be the most numerous of them in followers on the Day of Resurrection."
3) The noble Qur'an is mercy and a reminder, that is, a lesson and admonition for those who believe in it and for those upon whom it was sent down.

4) Establishing the loss of the polytheists in both abodes, for their exchanging falsehood for truth, and we seek refuge in Allah, the Exalted.

**Explanation of terms:**

*Yastaʿjilūnaka bil-ʿadhāb*: they ask you to hasten the punishment for them, i.e., they demand that the punishment be brought to them quickly.

*Wa-lawlā ajalun musammā*: i.e., a specified time for the punishment that neither precedes nor follows it, would have come to them.

*Wa-la-yaʾtiyannahum baghtatan*: suddenly, from where they do not expect it.

*Wa-inna jahannama la-muḥīṭatun bil-kāfirīn*: i.e., encompassing them on every side while they are in it; and that is the day it covers them.

*Yawma yaghshāhumu al-ʿadhāb*: i.e., from above them and from beneath their feet.

*Dhūqū mā kuntum taʿmalūn*: i.e., the Almighty says to them: "Taste what you used to do," namely of shirk and sins.

**Meaning of the verses:**

It has already been mentioned in the preceding verses that those who denied the Muhammadan message demanded the punishment as a challenge to the Messenger ﷺ, saying: "Bring us the punishment if you are among the truthful in claiming that you are a prophet and messenger to us." In this verse, the Exalted instructs His Messenger, i.e., leads him to marvel at the folly, levity and misguidance of the polytheists, as they demand the punishment. So He says to him: ﴿They ask you to hasten the punishment, and had there not been a specified term for it, i.e., a set time that neither precedes nor follows it, ﴾ ﴿the punishment would have come to them.﴾ Then the Exalted informed His Messenger, emphasizing His statement, saying: ﴿And it will surely come upon them﴾, i.e., the punishment, ﴿suddenly﴾ without doubt, ﴿while they do not perceive﴾ the time of its coming. Then the Exalted again directed His Messenger to marvel at the foolishness of the polytheists, who cannot endure the sting of a scorpion or the bite of a viper, yet demand the punishment. So He says: ﴿They ask you to hasten the punishment, and indeed Hell encompasses the disbelievers﴾ without doubt, like His saying: ﴿The command of Allah has come﴾ [al-Naḥl: 1]. ﴿On the Day the punishment will cover them﴾, i.e., envelop and overwhelm them, so that it will be ﴿from above them and from beneath their feet.﴾ Hell encompasses them, and the Almighty, Blessed and Exalted, says, rebuking them: ﴿Taste what you used to do﴾ of shirk and sins.

From the guidance of these verses:

1) The permissibility of marvelling when its causes that prompt it are present.

2) Clarification of the extent of the foolishness, ignorance and levity of the disbelievers and polytheists in particular.

3) Clarification that the delay of the punishment was not due to incapacity, but rather to a precise order, since everything has a specified term that neither precedes nor follows it.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 29, verses 56–60:

Explanation of the words:

"Indeed My earth is vast" (inna ardi wasi'a): that is, emigrate from lands where you cannot worship, for indeed God's earth is vast.

"So worship Me alone" (fa-iyaya fa'budun): worship Me alone and do not worship others along with Me, as the polytheists want you to do.

"Every soul shall taste death" (kullu nafsin dha'iqatu al-mawt): that is, let not the fear of death prevent you from emigrating in the way of God, for death is inevitable for the emigrants and for those who abandon emigration.

"Then to Us you will be returned" (thumma ilayna turja'un): that is, after your death you will be returned to God. Whoever dies seeking His good pleasure, He honours and makes him happy; whoever dies in disobedience to Him, He makes him taste His punishment.

"We will surely settle them" (linubawwi'annahum): that is, We will surely make them dwell in Paradise in lofty chambers beneath which rivers flow.

"Those who were patient" (alladhina sabaru): that is, they were patient in faith and in emigration, relying upon God, exalted is He.

"And how many a creature carries not its provision" (wa-ka'ayyin min da'abbatin la tahmilu rizqaha): that is, it is not able to gather it or carry it because of its weakness, yet God provides for it; so there is no excuse for one who abandons emigration out of fear of hunger and destitution.

"And He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing" (wa-huwa al-sami' al-'alim): that is, the All-Hearing of the words of His servants, the All-Knowing of their intentions, their states, and their deeds.

Meaning of the verses:

There is no doubt that after this divine reproach of the polytheists, their threat with punishment, and their rebuke with the Fire of Hell for their polytheism and falsehood, the reaction of the polytheists was to press upon the weak believers in Makkah. So God, exalted is He, guided them to emigrate from Makkah to Madinah so that they could worship God. He called them with His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O My servants who have believed﴾, meaning, in Me, My Messenger, and My meeting, ﴿indeed My earth is vast﴾, so emigrate therein, and do not accept remaining with disbelief, being humiliated and compelled to worship other than Me, the gods of the polytheists. ﴿So worship Me alone﴾, do not worship others along with Me.

Accordingly, emigrate in the way of My good pleasure, and do not fear death or poverty, for ﴿every soul shall taste death﴾ whether its owner emigrates or does not emigrate. And His saying: ﴿Then to Us you will be returned﴾ is certain. Whoever returns to Us while he is a believer, obedient, carrying out Our commands and avoiding Our prohibitions, We make happy; and whoever returns to Us while he is a disbeliever, disobedient to Us, neglecting Our commands and committing Our prohibitions, We make wretched. And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And those who believed and did righteous deeds – We will surely settle them in the Paradise, lofty chambers beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever﴾, that is, We will surely make them dwell in Paradise, the abode of happiness, ﴿lofty chambers beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever﴾, that is, they do not leave it nor do they die therein. This is an explanation of the reward of one who dies while a believer doing righteous deeds, among them emigration in the way of God. And His saying: ﴿How excellent is the reward of the workers﴾, that is, that settling in the chambers of the gardens is the happiness that follows from faith, emigration, and righteous deeds; faith, emigration, and righteous deeds are the work, and Paradise with its bliss is the wage for that work. God exalted Paradise, saying: ﴿How excellent is the reward of the workers﴾, and He described them with His saying: ﴿who were patient﴾, that is, in faith, emigration, and obedience, ﴿and upon their Lord they rely﴾. So they left their homes, leaving their wealth, carrying no provisions with them, all of this out of reliance upon their Lord. And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And how many a creature carries not its provision﴾ because of its weakness and incapacity, that is, many animals, of humans and beasts, are unable even to carry their food or drink because of their weakness, yet God, exalted is He, provides for them through the means He subjects for them and the opportunities He arranges, so they eat and drink like the strong and capable. Accordingly, let not the fear of hunger and poverty prevent you from emigrating, for God has guaranteed your provision and the provision of all His creatures.

﴿And He is the All-Hearing﴾ of your words, ﴿the All-Knowing﴾ of your inner and outer states, your deeds and your conditions. So fear Him and do not fear other than Him, for in obedience to Him is happiness and perfection, and in disobedience to Him is wretchedness and loss.

Guidance of the verses:

1) No one has an excuse for abandoning the worship of God and His monotheism, for if he is prevented from it in one land, he is obligated to emigrate to another land.

2) There is no sense in fearing death when action such as emigration and jihad is required, for death is a truth and inevitable.

3) A statement of the reward of the people of patience and reliance upon God, from among the people of faith, emigration, and piety.

4) The believer should not be prevented from emigration by fear of hunger in the land of his emigration, since God has guaranteed his provision.

**Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 29, verses 61–64**

**Explanation of the words:**

﴿And if you asked them﴾: i.e., the polytheists.

﴿And subjected the sun and the moon﴾: i.e., made them subservient, moving through all time without tiring or slowing.

﴿Then how are they turned away?﴾: i.e., how are they diverted from the truth after its proofs have become clear to them? The proof is that the Creator who governs is the true God, the One who must be made One (tawhid) in worship.

﴿Allah extends provision to whom He wills﴾: i.e., He widens provision for whichever of His servants He wills, as a test for the servant, to see whether he gives thanks to Allah or denies His blessings.

﴿And restricts it for him﴾: i.e., and He constricts it upon him, as a trial, to see whether he is patient or resentful.

﴿And if you asked them, "Who sends down water from the sky and gives life thereby to the earth after its death?" they would surely say, "Allah."﴾ Then how do they associate with Him idols that neither benefit nor harm?

﴿Say, "All praise is for Allah."﴾: i.e., say to them, "All praise is for Allah," for the proof has been established against you.

﴿But most of them do not reason.﴾: i.e., they are inconsistent in their understanding and in their answers.

﴿And this worldly life is nothing but amusement and play.﴾: i.e., in relation to working for it and living in it, it is amusement with which a person diverts himself, and play from which he gains nothing useful or of benefit.

﴿And indeed, the Hereafter is the [true] life.﴾: i.e., the complete, eternal life; therefore working for it is better than working for this world.

﴿If only they knew.﴾: i.e., if the polytheists knew this, they would not have preferred the perishable world over the enduring Hereafter.

**The meaning of the verses:**

The discourse continues to establish tawhid (affirmation of Allah's oneness), to denounce shirk (associating partners with Allah), and to remind the polytheists, in the hope that they might believe in Allah's oneness. Allah, Exalted, says to His Messenger (ﷺ): ﴿And if you asked them﴾, i.e., if you asked these polytheists, who harm the believers and persecute them for their monotheism towards Allah, if you asked them ﴿who created the heavens and the earth﴾, i.e., who brought them into existence from nothingness, and who subjected the sun and the moon in their orbits, moving through all of life, they would surely answer you, saying, "Allah." ﴿Then how are they turned away?﴾, i.e., how are they diverted from the truth after its proofs have become clear? This is a state that calls for wonder.

His saying, Exalted: ﴿Allah extends provision to whom He wills of His servants and restricts it for him﴾, is a manifestation of divine wisdom and wise governance, and it necessitates divinity for Him and negates it from anything other than Him. This one is given expanded provision, so He widens for him his food, drink, clothing, mount and dwelling; and that one is constricted in those things. Why? The answer is that He widens as a test for the servant, to see whether he gives thanks or denies, and He constricts as a trial for the servant, to see whether he is patient or resentful. Therefore the polytheists have no argument in the wealth of some and the poverty of believers. Wealth does not indicate Allah's pleasure with the servant, nor His displeasure; likewise poverty does not indicate displeasure or pleasure. His saying, Exalted: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Knowing of all things﴾, establishes His wisdom, mercy, justice and governance. He widens for one wisdom and constricts for another, because of His knowledge of His servants and what benefits or corrupts them. For some people wealth is what benefits them, and for others poverty is what benefits them; and likewise with what corrupts them.

His saying, Exalted: ﴿And if you asked them, "Who sends down water from the sky and gives life thereby to the earth after its death?"﴾, i.e., and if you asked them, O Our Messenger, these polytheists, saying: "Who sends down water, the rain, from the sky and gives life thereby to the earth after it had died from drought and barrenness?" they would surely answer you, saying: "Allah." Then say to them: "All praise is for Allah," for your acknowledgment of the truth. Yet you would act in accordance with its requirements. Since Allah is the One who sends down water and gives life to the earth after its death, worship is therefore due to Him alone. Why, then, do you worship other gods alongside Him, which send down no water, give life to no earth, and do nothing else? ﴿But most of them do not reason﴾, for if they reasoned they would not have associated stones and idols with their Lord, nor would they have been so inconsistent in their statements and actions: they acknowledge Allah as Lord, Creator, Provider and Governor, yet they bow down before idols, call upon them for help, invoke them, and show enmity towards, and even fight, whoever forbids them from that.

His saying, Exalted: ﴿And this worldly life is not but amusement and play﴾, i.e., the life that has blinded people from the Hereafter and diverted them from preparing for it: what is it? It is nothing but amusement and play. The unbeliever busies himself with it, works for it night and day, then dies and departs from it empty-handed, like children who play all day and then return with nothing except the fatigue they have incurred. It is obligatory to turn this life into righteous, fruitful work with which the servant provisions himself for his Hereafter, since the Hereafter is the [true] life, i.e., the complete, eternal life. For it the workers work, and in its pursuit competitors compete. This is the meaning of His saying, Exalted: ﴿And indeed, the Hereafter — that is the [true] life﴾, i.e., the Hereafter is the life for which we must work, because of its permanence and excellence. His saying: ﴿If only they knew﴾, i.e., yes, if they had known that the Hereafter is better, they would not have turned towards this world and turned away from the Hereafter. But their ignorance is the cause of their turning away, so their remedy is knowledge.

**Guidance from these verses:**

1) Wonder at the inconsistency of the polytheists, who affirm Allah's lordship (rububiyyah) yet deny His divinity (uluhiyyah).

2) Clarification of the fact that wealth and poverty indicate neither Allah's pleasure nor His displeasure, but rather His knowledge, His wisdom and His good governance.

3) Demonstration of the worthlessness and triviality of this world and the greatness and high value of the Hereafter. Therefore the most foolish and most senseless of people is the one who is blind to the Hereafter and disbelieves in it, while he sees this world and believes in it.

﴿And this worldly life is nothing but amusement and play.﴾: i.e., in relation to working for it and living in it, it is amusement with which a person diverts himself, and play from which he gains nothing useful or of benefit.

﴿And indeed, the Hereafter is the [true] life.﴾: i.e., the complete, eternal life; therefore working for it is better than working for this world.

﴿If only they knew.﴾: i.e., if the polytheists knew this, they would not have preferred the perishable world over the enduring Hereafter.

**The meaning of the verses:**

The discourse continues to establish tawhid (affirmation of Allah's oneness), to denounce shirk (associating partners with Allah), and to remind the polytheists, in the hope that they might believe in Allah's oneness. Allah, Exalted, says to His Messenger (ﷺ): ﴿And if you asked them﴾, i.e., if you asked these polytheists, who harm the believers and persecute them for their monotheism towards Allah, if you asked them ﴿who created the heavens and the earth﴾, i.e., who brought them into existence from nothingness, and who subjected the sun and the moon in their orbits, moving through all of life, they would surely answer you, saying, "Allah." ﴿Then how are they turned away?﴾, i.e., how are they diverted from the truth after its proofs have become clear? This is a state that calls for wonder.

His saying, Exalted: ﴿Allah extends provision to whom He wills of His servants and restricts it for him﴾, is a manifestation of divine wisdom and wise governance, and it necessitates divinity for Him and negates it from anything other than Him. This one is given expanded provision, so He widens for him his food, drink, clothing, mount and dwelling; and that one is constricted in those things. Why? The answer is that He widens as a test for the servant, to see whether he gives thanks or denies, and He constricts as a trial for the servant, to see whether he is patient or resentful. Therefore the polytheists have no argument in the wealth of some and the poverty of believers. Wealth does not indicate Allah's pleasure with the servant, nor His displeasure; likewise poverty does not indicate displeasure or pleasure. His saying, Exalted: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Knowing of all things﴾, establishes His wisdom, mercy, justice and governance. He widens for one wisdom and constricts for another, because of His knowledge of His servants and what benefits or corrupts them. For some people wealth is what benefits them, and for others poverty is what benefits them; and likewise with what corrupts them.

His saying, Exalted: ﴿And if you asked them, "Who sends down water from the sky and gives life thereby to the earth after its death?"﴾, i.e., and if you asked them, O Our Messenger, these polytheists, saying: "Who sends down water, the rain, from the sky and gives life thereby to the earth after it had died from drought and barrenness?" they would surely answer you, saying: "Allah." Then say to them: "All praise is for Allah," for your acknowledgment of the truth. Yet you would act in accordance with its requirements. Since Allah is the One who sends down water and gives life to the earth after its death, worship is therefore due to Him alone. Why, then, do you worship other gods alongside Him, which send down no water, give life to no earth, and do nothing else? ﴿But most of them do not reason﴾, for if they reasoned they would not have associated stones and idols with their Lord, nor would they have been so inconsistent in their statements and actions: they acknowledge Allah as Lord, Creator, Provider and Governor, yet they bow down before idols, call upon them for help, invoke them, and show enmity towards, and even fight, whoever forbids them from that.

His saying, Exalted: ﴿And this worldly life is not but amusement and play﴾, i.e., the life that has blinded people from the Hereafter and diverted them from preparing for it: what is it? It is nothing but amusement and play. The unbeliever busies himself with it, works for it night and day, then dies and departs from it empty-handed, like children who play all day and then return with nothing except the fatigue they have incurred. It is obligatory to turn this life into righteous, fruitful work with which the servant provisions himself for his Hereafter, since the Hereafter is the [true] life, i.e., the complete, eternal life. For it the workers work, and in its pursuit competitors compete. This is the meaning of His saying, Exalted: ﴿And indeed, the Hereafter — that is the [true] life﴾, i.e., the Hereafter is the life for which we must work, because of its permanence and excellence. His saying: ﴿If only they knew﴾, i.e., yes, if they had known that the Hereafter is better, they would not have turned towards this world and turned away from the Hereafter. But their ignorance is the cause of their turning away, so their remedy is knowledge.

**Guidance from these verses:**

1) Wonder at the inconsistency of the polytheists, who affirm Allah's lordship (rububiyyah) yet deny His divinity (uluhiyyah).

2) Clarification of the fact that wealth and poverty indicate neither Allah's pleasure nor His displeasure, but rather His knowledge, His wisdom and His good governance.

3) Demonstration of the worthlessness and triviality of this world and the greatness and high value of the Hereafter. Therefore the most foolish and most senseless of people is the one who is blind to the Hereafter and disbelieves in it, while he sees this world and believes in it.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 29, verses 65–69:

Explanation of the words:

"في الفلك" (fi al-fulk): i.e., in the ship.

"مخلصين له الدين" (mukhlisina lahu al-din): i.e., they called upon Allah alone and did not mention any other deities along with Him.

"إذا هم يشركون" (idha hum yushrikun): i.e., they suddenly ascribe partners to Him, which is calling upon other than Allah, exalted is He.

"ليكفروا بما آتيناهم" (liyakfuru bima atynahum): i.e., by the blessing of deliverance from drowning and other blessings.

"فسوف يعلمون" (fasawfa ya'lamun): i.e., they will come to know the outcome of their disbelief when they are cast into Hell.

"ويتخطف الناس من حولهم" (wa yutakhattafu al-nas min hawlihim): i.e., they are taken captive and killed in the lands of their peninsula.

"أفبالباطل يؤمنون" (afa bil-batil yu'minun): i.e., they believe in idols, which are falsehood; Allah, exalted is He, rebukes them for this.

"والذين جاهدوا فينا" (wal-ladhina jahadu fina): i.e., they exerted their effort in correcting their beliefs, purifying their souls and refining their character, and then by fighting the enemies of Allah from among the disbelievers who wage war against Islam and the Muslims.

"لنهدينهم سبلنا" (lanahdiyannahum subulana): i.e., We will surely enable them to know what leads to Our love and Our pleasure, and We will help them attain it.

Explanation of the context:

The noble context continues to denounce the polytheists and their polytheism. It has already been mentioned in the context that they acknowledge the lordship of Allah, for if they were asked who created the heavens and the earth and subjected the sun and the moon, they would say "Allah," and if they were asked who sent down water from the sky and thereby gave life to the earth after its death, they would say "Allah." Yet, despite this, they ascribe to Allah idols as partners. Just as they acknowledge the lordship of Allah and then associate idols with Him, when they board a ship, i.e., one of the vessels, and waves come upon them, tossing them about, and they fear drowning, they call upon Allah, exalted is He, ﴿sincere to Him in religion﴾, i.e., in supplication, asking Him alone, to the exclusion of their deities, to deliver them from drowning. ﴿But when He delivers them to the land﴾, and they disembark safe from drowning, ﴿behold, they associate partners﴾, i.e., they suddenly ascribe partners to Him. This contradiction on their part is like the contradiction in their acknowledgment of the lordship of Allah and then their associating others with Him. The source of this lies in ignorance, blind imitation, obstinacy, denial, and arrogance. This is what the first verse of this context indicates, namely His saying: ﴿So when they board the ship, they call upon Allah, sincere to Him in religion. But when He delivers them to the land, behold, they associate partners.﴾

As for His saying in verse [66]: ﴿so that they may deny what We have given them﴾, i.e., their return to polytheism after their deliverance from drowning and their arrival on land was as if it were for the purpose of denying the blessing of Allah in delivering them from drowning; for had they not denied it, they would have continued to be sincere to Allah in supplication and worship, worshipping Him alone without the deities they had abandoned at the onset of hardship and the confrontation with calamity. And His saying: ﴿and that they may enjoy themselves﴾ is read with a sukun on the lam, and Ibn Jarir preferred this reading, so the meaning is: and that they may enjoy in their worldly life what Allah has given them of the enjoyment of the life of this world; ﴿but they will soon know﴾ the outcome of that after their death, which is the punishment of the Hereafter, and the command in His saying "and let them enjoy" is then one of threat and warning.

As for the reading with a kasra on the lam in "wa liyatamatta'u," the clause is then conjoined to His saying "liyakfuru," i.e., they were sincere in hardship and associated partners in ease, so that they might disbelieve and enjoy what they were given in life. That would not benefit them, nor would it avail them anything against Allah; ﴿so they will soon know﴾ the punishment that will befall them and the calamity and wretchedness that will descend upon them.

As for His saying in the third verse [67]: ﴿Have they not seen that We made a sanctuary secure, while people are being snatched away from around them?﴾, i.e., have those polytheists, who were ungrateful for the blessing of Allah in delivering them from drowning, not seen another blessing, namely that Allah, exalted is He, made for them a secure sanctuary in which they dwell safe from the raids of enemies and the wars of oppressors and transgressors, no one assaulting them within their sanctuary nor wronging them; whereas the people around them, in the outskirts and midst of their peninsula, are being snatched away: raids are launched against them, and they are killed and taken captive at every time and moment. Is this not one of the greatest blessings, one that demands their thanks to Allah by worshipping Him and abandoning the worship of anything besides Him? Therefore Allah, exalted is He, said, rebuking them and condemning their conduct: ﴿Then in falsehood do they believe?﴾, i.e., in polytheism and the worship of idols do they affirm and acknowledge, ﴿and in the blessing of Allah do they disbelieve?﴾, i.e., they deny the favor of their Lord upon them, and so do not thank Him by worshipping Him and affirming His oneness in worship.

As for His saying in the fourth verse [68]: ﴿And who is more unjust than one who invents a lie against Allah or denies the truth when it has come to him?﴾, He described them with extreme injustice in two respects: the first in their lying against Allah by forbidding what He permitted, permitting what He forbade, and taking partners with Allah, claiming that they intercede for them with Allah, Mighty and Majestic; and the second in their denial of the truth that the Messenger of Allah brought to them, namely the Islamic religion with its beliefs and laws, for they denied the Qur'an and the Messenger (ﷺ). After this recording of the greatest injustice committed by them, Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Is there not in Hell an abode for the disbelievers?﴾ The interrogation is for affirmation, i.e., indeed in Hell there is an abode, a dwelling, for disbelievers like them, who are disbelieving and unjust, and that is their recompense; and what an evil recompense is Hell.

As for His saying in the fifth verse [69]: ﴿And those who strive in Us, We will surely guide them to Our paths. And indeed Allah is with the doers of good﴾, in this verse is a joyful glad tidings and a generous, true promise. That is because whoever strives in the way of Allah, i.e., seeking the pleasure of Allah by working to raise His word, so that He is worshipped and nothing besides Him is worshipped, fighting the polytheists on the day when permission to fight them is granted, Allah, exalted is He, will guide him, i.e., enable him, to the path of salvation from what is feared and to success in attaining what is loved. And whoever strives for the sake of Allah against his own self, his desire, Satan and his allies, this glad tiding reaches him and this promise is fulfilled for him, for Allah is with the doers of good, by His help, support and aid against those whom they strive against in the way of Allah. What is meant by the doers of good are those who make their intentions, deeds and words good, so that they become righteous and fruitful for the purification of their souls and the cleansing of their spirits. O Allah, make us among them, and grant us what You have promised them, for You are Generous and Bountiful.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1) Clarification that the Arab polytheists were not atheists who did not believe in Allah, and affirmation that they were monotheists in lordship (tawhid al-rububiyyah) but polytheists in divinity, i.e., worship (tawhid al-uluhiyyah).

2) Awakening the consciences of the polytheists by reminding them of the blessings of Allah upon them, perhaps they will be thankful.

3) There is no injustice greater than that of one who fabricates lies against Allah and denies the truth when it has come to him, has reached him and he has recognized it, yet turns away from it, preferring his worldly life and following his desires.

4) The glad tidings from Allah to whoever strives against the polytheists and strives against his own self, desire and the devils, of being guided to the path of success and salvation in this world and the Hereafter.

5) The virtue of ihsan (excellence), which is sincerity in worship to Allah and performing it perfectly and beautifully as Allah has prescribed, and the demonstration of this virtue lies in Allah being with the doers of good by supporting them, aiding them, bestowing favors upon them and honoring them in His generous presence.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 29, verses 65–69:

Explanation of the words:

"في الفلك" (fi al-fulk): i.e., in the ship.

"مخلصين له الدين" (mukhlisina lahu al-din): i.e., they called upon Allah alone and did not mention any other deities along with Him.

"إذا هم يشركون" (idha hum yushrikun): i.e., they suddenly ascribe partners to Him, which is calling upon other than Allah, exalted is He.

"ليكفروا بما آتيناهم" (liyakfuru bima atynahum): i.e., by the blessing of deliverance from drowning and other blessings.

"فسوف يعلمون" (fasawfa ya'lamun): i.e., they will come to know the outcome of their disbelief when they are cast into Hell.

"ويتخطف الناس من حولهم" (wa yutakhattafu al-nas min hawlihim): i.e., they are taken captive and killed in the lands of their peninsula.

"أفبالباطل يؤمنون" (afa bil-batil yu'minun): i.e., they believe in idols, which are falsehood; Allah, exalted is He, rebukes them for this.

"والذين جاهدوا فينا" (wal-ladhina jahadu fina): i.e., they exerted their effort in correcting their beliefs, purifying their souls and refining their character, and then by fighting the enemies of Allah from among the disbelievers who wage war against Islam and the Muslims.

"لنهدينهم سبلنا" (lanahdiyannahum subulana): i.e., We will surely enable them to know what leads to Our love and Our pleasure, and We will help them attain it.

Explanation of the context:

The noble context continues to denounce the polytheists and their polytheism. It has already been mentioned in the context that they acknowledge the lordship of Allah, for if they were asked who created the heavens and the earth and subjected the sun and the moon, they would say "Allah," and if they were asked who sent down water from the sky and thereby gave life to the earth after its death, they would say "Allah." Yet, despite this, they ascribe to Allah idols as partners. Just as they acknowledge the lordship of Allah and then associate idols with Him, when they board a ship, i.e., one of the vessels, and waves come upon them, tossing them about, and they fear drowning, they call upon Allah, exalted is He, ﴿sincere to Him in religion﴾, i.e., in supplication, asking Him alone, to the exclusion of their deities, to deliver them from drowning. ﴿But when He delivers them to the land﴾, and they disembark safe from drowning, ﴿behold, they associate partners﴾, i.e., they suddenly ascribe partners to Him. This contradiction on their part is like the contradiction in their acknowledgment of the lordship of Allah and then their associating others with Him. The source of this lies in ignorance, blind imitation, obstinacy, denial, and arrogance. This is what the first verse of this context indicates, namely His saying: ﴿So when they board the ship, they call upon Allah, sincere to Him in religion. But when He delivers them to the land, behold, they associate partners.﴾

As for His saying in verse [66]: ﴿so that they may deny what We have given them﴾, i.e., their return to polytheism after their deliverance from drowning and their arrival on land was as if it were for the purpose of denying the blessing of Allah in delivering them from drowning; for had they not denied it, they would have continued to be sincere to Allah in supplication and worship, worshipping Him alone without the deities they had abandoned at the onset of hardship and the confrontation with calamity. And His saying: ﴿and that they may enjoy themselves﴾ is read with a sukun on the lam, and Ibn Jarir preferred this reading, so the meaning is: and that they may enjoy in their worldly life what Allah has given them of the enjoyment of the life of this world; ﴿but they will soon know﴾ the outcome of that after their death, which is the punishment of the Hereafter, and the command in His saying "and let them enjoy" is then one of threat and warning.

As for the reading with a kasra on the lam in "wa liyatamatta'u," the clause is then conjoined to His saying "liyakfuru," i.e., they were sincere in hardship and associated partners in ease, so that they might disbelieve and enjoy what they were given in life. That would not benefit them, nor would it avail them anything against Allah; ﴿so they will soon know﴾ the punishment that will befall them and the calamity and wretchedness that will descend upon them.

As for His saying in the third verse [67]: ﴿Have they not seen that We made a sanctuary secure, while people are being snatched away from around them?﴾, i.e., have those polytheists, who were ungrateful for the blessing of Allah in delivering them from drowning, not seen another blessing, namely that Allah, exalted is He, made for them a secure sanctuary in which they dwell safe from the raids of enemies and the wars of oppressors and transgressors, no one assaulting them within their sanctuary nor wronging them; whereas the people around them, in the outskirts and midst of their peninsula, are being snatched away: raids are launched against them, and they are killed and taken captive at every time and moment. Is this not one of the greatest blessings, one that demands their thanks to Allah by worshipping Him and abandoning the worship of anything besides Him? Therefore Allah, exalted is He, said, rebuking them and condemning their conduct: ﴿Then in falsehood do they believe?﴾, i.e., in polytheism and the worship of idols do they affirm and acknowledge, ﴿and in the blessing of Allah do they disbelieve?﴾, i.e., they deny the favor of their Lord upon them, and so do not thank Him by worshipping Him and affirming His oneness in worship.

As for His saying in the fourth verse [68]: ﴿And who is more unjust than one who invents a lie against Allah or denies the truth when it has come to him?﴾, He described them with extreme injustice in two respects: the first in their lying against Allah by forbidding what He permitted, permitting what He forbade, and taking partners with Allah, claiming that they intercede for them with Allah, Mighty and Majestic; and the second in their denial of the truth that the Messenger of Allah brought to them, namely the Islamic religion with its beliefs and laws, for they denied the Qur'an and the Messenger (ﷺ). After this recording of the greatest injustice committed by them, Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Is there not in Hell an abode for the disbelievers?﴾ The interrogation is for affirmation, i.e., indeed in Hell there is an abode, a dwelling, for disbelievers like them, who are disbelieving and unjust, and that is their recompense; and what an evil recompense is Hell.

As for His saying in the fifth verse [69]: ﴿And those who strive in Us, We will surely guide them to Our paths. And indeed Allah is with the doers of good﴾, in this verse is a joyful glad tidings and a generous, true promise. That is because whoever strives in the way of Allah, i.e., seeking the pleasure of Allah by working to raise His word, so that He is worshipped and nothing besides Him is worshipped, fighting the polytheists on the day when permission to fight them is granted, Allah, exalted is He, will guide him, i.e., enable him, to the path of salvation from what is feared and to success in attaining what is loved. And whoever strives for the sake of Allah against his own self, his desire, Satan and his allies, this glad tiding reaches him and this promise is fulfilled for him, for Allah is with the doers of good, by His help, support and aid against those whom they strive against in the way of Allah. What is meant by the doers of good are those who make their intentions, deeds and words good, so that they become righteous and fruitful for the purification of their souls and the cleansing of their spirits. O Allah, make us among them, and grant us what You have promised them, for You are Generous and Bountiful.
